events.id: Anthonie Tonnon Presents Cinematographer | Wellington (Late Show)-Hannah Playhouse,12 Cambridge Ter, Te Aro, Wellington 6011, New Zealand, Wellington-All Events In
events.name: Anthonie Tonnon Presents Cinematographer | Wellington (Late Show)
events.venue: Hannah Playhouse,12 Cambridge Ter, Te Aro, Wellington 6011, New Zealand, Wellington
events.long_description:
Anthonie Tonnon Presents Cinematographer | Wellington (Late Show)
Taite Music Prize-winning songwriter Anthonie Tonnon presents his immersive new live show, Cinematographer.

Three years in the making, Cinematographer combines live electronic music, cinematic storytelling and visual design into an immersive performance. Featuring visual DJing by Erica Sklenars, videography by Theo Taylor, styling by Karlya Smith and design by Daniel Alexander, the show sees Tonnon playing the roles of DJ, singer, documentarian and revolutionary lecturer.

The show explores two timelines: the Situationist International in France and Italy during the 1960s, and Whanganui, New Zealand at the turn of the millennium - a mysterious, forgotten city where a new battle is being waged against what Guy Debord famously called The Society of the Spectacle.

Swapping his guitar for a vocoder, and transforming two Synthstrom Deluges into honorary turntables, Tonnon connects these seemingly distant worlds through the musical language of turn-of-the-millennium dance culture.

"Cinematographer is part film, part francophile performance lecture, part disco club set," says Tonnon. "It's a world that we've built for this new music, exploring some newfound passions – the French avant-garde, cinema, urban politics of the 1960s, turn-of-the-millennium dance culture and documentary films, and the glorious, mystifying city of Whanganui."

The ambitious audiovisual performance introduces an entirely new body of work developed with Tonnon's band and longtime producer Jonathan Pearce. The new single and video "Executive Assistant" offers the first glimpse into this new world - Tonnon's first new music in three years.

Doors open: 8.45PM I Show 9:15PM

Unallocated seating and standing available.

Early Bird tickets available until Monday 10 August or until allocation sells out.

events.id: 100 Years of Unity through Sport — New Zealand and India-Frank Kitts Park, Wellington, New Zealand-Wellington NZ
events.name: 100 Years of Unity through Sport — New Zealand and India
events.venue: Frank Kitts Park, Wellington, New Zealand
events.long_description:
This spring, Wellington will celebrate 100 years of sporting connection between India and New Zealand. The city will showcase its strong Indian community and cultural connections. This century milestone traces back to 1926, when an Indian Army hockey team toured New Zealand for the first time, bringing players and communities together. Since then, sport has played an important role in connecting our countries — notably through hockey and cricket, but also across many other sports and exchanges. 

From 23 October to 15 November, Frank Kitts Park and the waterfront promenade will host a free public exhibition. Light Box Historic Walk will feature 10 illuminated light boxes that share stories of Wellington-specific links between India and New Zealand. You’ll also find The Fan Hub on 6 and 7 November as well as 14 and 15 November. Enjoy a feast with local food truck favourites, offering a taste of Wellington's rich culinary scene. Or start the day with sunrise yoga sessions hosted by AWHI Yoga against the stunning waterfront backdrop. To cap off all the excitement, the BLACKCAPS take on India three times in Wellington as part of their summer season.

The Sport100 Fan Hub is proudly delivered through collaboration between WellingtonNZ, Sport New Zealand, Wellington City Council, Cricket Wellington, and New Zealand Cricket, creating a festive gathering place for locals and visitors to connect, celebrate, and enjoy the atmosphere whilst Wellington hosts cricketing giants India in the capital.

events.id: Cornelia Parker-City Gallery Wellington-Wellington NZ
events.name: Cornelia Parker
events.venue: City Gallery Wellington
events.long_description:
After three years of closure, the newly renovated and strengthened City Gallery Wellington Te Whare Toi will host the art of Cornelia Parker. The British visual artist is best known for her innovative and contemporary sculpture and installation art. Her large-scale, immersive installations explore themes of destruction and reconstruction, transformation and metamorphosis. Objects are exploded, crushed, and suspended in a world upended and remade anew.
Curated by independent UK-based curator Andrea Schlieker and City Gallery Wellington’s Senior Curator Aaron Lister, City Gallery Wellington’s exhibition will encompass Parker’s long career as an artist. This includes an immersive sound-and-light installation, ‘Stolen Thunder’. The work gathers the sounds of approaching storms from around the globe and across time. The exhibition will also showcase her paintings, photos, films, and sculptures.
“I have always said this is the one exhibition I want to do before I die,” said Charlotte Davy, Ringatohu Toi Director, Art and City Gallery Wellington. “I have been following Cornelia Parker’s work for the last twenty years. Bringing her mischievous, dark, and literally explosive work to Wellington is incredible.” 
Parker’s work often fills entire rooms and invites the viewer to move through and around the art. Given its physical scale, the blank canvas of the reopened gallery offers the perfect opportunity to host the exhibition. The exhibition will kick off in October 2026 and run through March 2027. 
Charlotte notes the exhibition’s themes are also of particular relevance to Wellington. “I hope that the exhibition and our return to Te Ngākau Civic Square will reflect our city and also help remake it. We are looking forward to opening with a bang.”
Hero image: © Cornelia Parker. Courtesy of the artist and Frith Street Gallery, London

Presented by: SBM Presents
Killswitch Engage return to New Zealand in 2026, bringing more than two decades of genre-defining metal to the stage with their biggest Antipodean headline shows yet, joined by special guests Sylosis. The Western Massachusetts heavyweights helped redraw the map for modern metal in the early 2000s, fusing blistering European-inspired guitar work, East Coast hardcore energy and emotionally charged, uplifting lyrics into a sound that changed the game for a generation of bands and fans.
Across a landmark career, Killswitch Engage have earned three Grammy nominations for Best Metal Performance, multiple gold and platinum records, billions of streams and a reputation as one of the most powerful live acts in heavy music. From classic albums like Alive Or Just Breathing, The End of Heartache and As Daylight Dies through to chart-topping releases Disarm the Descent, Incarnate and 2019’s Atonement, they’ve consistently raised the bar while packing out venues and festival main stages around the world.
Fresh from celebrating 25 years as a band and the release of their latest album This Consequence – featuring the blockbuster single “I Believe,” the biggest radio hit of their career – Killswitch Engage are set to deliver a career-spanning set for their New Zealand fans.
Expect a night that runs from era-defining anthems to new favourites, all delivered with the intensity and heart that has seen them share stages with everyone from Iron Maiden and Slayer to My Chemical Romance, Mastodon, Slipknot and Parkway Drive.

Across a landmark career, Killswitch Engage have earned three Grammy nominations for Best Metal Performance, multiple gold and platinum records, billions of streams and a reputation as one of the most powerful live acts in heavy music.
From classic albums like Alive Or Just Breathing, The End of Heartache and As Daylight Dies through to chart-topping releases Disarm the Descent, Incarnate and 2019’s Atonement, they’ve consistently raised the bar while packing out venues and festival main stages around the world.
Fresh from celebrating 25 years as a band and the release of their latest album This Consequence – featuring the blockbuster single “I Believe,” the biggest radio hit of their career – Killswitch Engage are set to deliver a career-spanning set for their New Zealand fans.

events.long_description:
Inside Circa Theatre’s waterfront venue, you’ll find two performance spaces. Both offer a smorgasbord of professional theatre throughout the year. Playwrights from international heavy hitters to brilliant Kiwi voices are represented. It also includes programming from comedies and cabarets to contemporary dance and pantomime. 
Before or after your show, visit the on-site café, brasserie and restaurant, Chouchou. It opens out onto a deck, where you can take in views across the harbour. Look up to admire the art installation above. Called ‘Velarium’, it undulates in the wind, mirroring the water in the harbour. 
Circa Theatre began its life in 1976. A breakaway group of actors and theatre practitioners decided that Aotearoa needed a new and innovative approach to theatre. Five decades later, it is still pushing boundaries, making people laugh and cry, and creating theatrical memories. 
If you don’t have your own Circa memory yet, there’s an opportunity to create one nearly every night of the week.

events.id: Porirua Parkrun-Bothamley Park, Champion Street, Porirua - Mana-Event Finder
events.name: Porirua Parkrun
events.venue: Bothamley Park, Champion Street, Porirua - Mana
events.long_description:
What is Porirua parkrun? It is a free 5km walk or run event - It’s not about coming first or winning. You can go at your own pace and just enjoy being with other people. It is inclusive and the perfect way to start your weekend in the outdoors chatting to people.

The start occurs just upstream of the Bothamley Park carpark. This car park is off Champion street, opposite the intersection with Windley Street. Head to end of carpark where the concrete ends and there is a gate. For location see https://goo.gl/maps/wEohfp9bRu82.

The course is following the old coach road (circa 1870's) established for the early farms in the area. Today this historic track is located within a park, away from cars and now used by walkers, runners and cyclists.

The track is generally 3 metres wide with a gentle gradient and a compacted gravel surface beside the Kenepuru Stream through a picturesque wooded wild valley. (Note there is a pinch point for a short section after the 2km marker where participants need to go single file each direction for approx 30 metres)

The valley runs east-west with mature trees which means this has to be one of the most sheltered places, out of the wind to exercise in Wellington.

What does it cost to join in? Nothing - it's free! but please register before your first run or walk, so you can get your timing results. You only need to register with parkrun once, to participate at any of the parkrun events around the world. Don't forget to bring a copy of your barcode. If you forget it, you won't get a time.

How fast do I have to be? Walking is fine as long as you can finish the 5km. Please come along and join in whatever your pace!

One dog per adult is welcome, as long as it is on a short hand held lead.

Children welcome but those 10 years and under need to be kept within arms reach of a supervising adult.

Note there is no toilets in the park, so go before you go.

We're friendly! Every week we grab a post park run/walk coffee/tea at Get Fixed within Kai Tahi at 20 Parumoana Street, to mix exercise with socialising.

There are volunteering opportunities even week. So those doing Duke of Edinburgh or similar challenges can get volunteer credits. Ensure you contact us well in advance at "porirua@parkrun.co.nz"

events.long_description:
AWHI Yoga and Wellbeing’s accredited 200hr YTT program is a comprehensive and thorough journey into becoming a 200 hr certified Yoga Teacher. We are the only vinyasa yoga teacher training in the world that blends Te Ao Māori and ancient yoga wisdoms, offering a uniquely 'Aotearoa' experience while retaining universal relevance for teaching and practicing yoga in any part of the world.

Our training is suitable for individuals interested in becoming a yoga teacher, or those looking to take a personal journey towards deepening your own practice and knowledge. Either way, we guarantee a transformative and life-changing experience that will deepen your relationship to yoga, others, Aotearoa and your self.

Our uniquely Aotearoa Teacher Training explores the beautiful marriage between ancient Yoga and Te Ao Māori teachings over five separate modules during our three months together. Our course follows the Māori hauora/wellbeing model of Te Whare Tapa Whā, which takes the same holistic view of health taken by traditional Yoga. As we work through each pillar we start tapping into something way greater than ourselves, enabling us to connect with our purpose in life and how we might share this in service to the world!

A $1,000 deposit reserves your spot.

events.id: Sunday Morning Jewellery-making In 4 Weeks - Mixed Level-Workspace Studios Wellington Market Lane, 3 Market Lane, Wellington Cenral, Wellington-Event Finder
events.name: Sunday Morning Jewellery-making In 4 Weeks - Mixed Level
events.venue: Workspace Studios Wellington Market Lane, 3 Market Lane, Wellington Cenral, Wellington
events.long_description:
Spend your Sunday mornings immersed in creativity, learning the timeless craft of jewellery-making in our warm, welcoming studio.

It runs from Sun 1 November for 4 weeks till Sun 22 November, 10am-1pm.

This short course is the perfect introduction for complete beginners, guiding you step-by-step through the essential techniques used by jewellers. You’ll start by working in copper or brass, building confidence as you learn to cut, heat, shape and texture metal. From there, you can choose to move into silver and bring your ideas to life in more refined pieces.

A beautiful textured ring band is an ideal first project, but once you’ve mastered the basics, the possibilities really open up—create earrings, pendants, or small bespoke pieces that reflect your personal style. You’ll learn how to solder using a jeweller’s torch, refine your finishing techniques, and polish your work to a professional shine. It’s a hands-on, deeply satisfying process, and there’s nothing quite like wearing something you’ve made yourself.

These Sunday sessions are also perfect for returning students and more experienced makers who want dedicated studio time, guidance on more ambitious projects, and the chance to be part of a friendly, creative community.

Materials are purchased as you go, so you can tailor your projects to your budget and ideas. Beginners typically spend around $50–$70 on metals over the course.

This block is ideal for teens and young creatives aged 12 and up. Please note: anyone under 16 must be accompanied by an enrolled parent or caregiver.

events.long_description:
Overview

Re-use, Re-Purpose, Beautify with Gold!! Come along and learn the magical art of Kintsugi with Artist Ema Frost in this new Workshop.

After several SOLD OUT workshops in Wellington here is the next one... Nov 2026

Learn the magical art of Kintsugi with Artist Ema Frost in this new Workshop. You can bring along a piece of your own pottery to restore in this beautiful style. (I'll also have a few as back up if you don't have your own piece) (All Levels)

Sunday 1st November - 10:30am - 12:30pm or 2 - 4pm




Ema Frost is a very clever Kiwi Artist, who has been teaching Kintsugi for 5+ years and regularly travels to Japan to study and learn new techniques. Ema's illustrations and ceramic works sit in many of our countries best galleries, and whose products and merchandise sell in the most stylish design stores and gallery shops. Her style is enchanting - quirky, feminine and colourful, and clearly influenced by her travels throughout the world, usually off the beaten track.

Have you ever wanted to try Kintsugi.... It's an ancient Japanese art form where you fix broken pottery with gold - making its imperfections its beauty. - A truly wonderful philosophy to live by. Nothing is ever really broken but new life and meaning is brought back making your piece a work of art and truly something special. You can also apply this technique on various materials like glass, wood, greenstone and shells.

KintsugiIt's called kintsugi (金継ぎ), or kintsukuroi (金繕い), literally golden (“kin”) and repair (“tsugi”). This traditional Japanese art uses a precious metal – liquid gold, liquid silver or lacquer dusted with powdered gold – to bring together the pieces of a broken pottery item and at the same time enhance the breaks.You will take away your wonderful finished work, plus your knew skills which will enable you to further your own Kintsugi in your own time.

What you will take away:A finished artwork pieceA understanding of KintsugiKnowledge and History of this beautiful art form.

Read less

events.long_description:
Located on beautiful and often windswept Pencarrow Head, New Zealand's oldest lighthouse dates to 1859.

Walk or cycle to Aotearoa's first lighthouse, then chat with knowledgeable guides about the history, construction and stories behind this unique Pōneke landmark, and explore the interior, usually restricted for public access.

Pencarrow Lighthouse open day is free to attend, however a koha is always appreciated.

Please note the track up to Pencarrow Lighthouse is steep and can be muddy. Ensure adequate footwear is worn. The weather can be changeable, and we recommend bring along snacks, water and a wind jacket. There are no toilets along the track up to Pencarrow Lighthouse or at the lighthouse itself. Public toilets are located near the end of Pencarrow Coast Road.

This event is proudly presented by Heritage New Zealand Pouhere Taonga as part of Wellington Heritage Festival 2026.

events.long_description:
Everyone is welcome to this fun class! Whether you have a little more experience, or are starting from scratch, if you want to draw people, this workshop is for you.

Here you will be closely tutored in how to draw people, from faces to anatomy, and you will learn technical skills while having fun in an encouraging environment.

In this class, artists will learn and extend their skills with drawing and painting.

Perfect for both beginners and more experienced artists, Ellie will help the students experiment and learn while having fun and creating wonderful pieces of art. Our classes builds self-confidence, traditional techniques, and creative experimentation.

They previously ran Tacit Art Gallery in Hamilton, and have worked at both the Waikato Museum and the Adam Art Gallery.

This event is a fun, safe space for all, including LGBTQ+ and the site includes a gender-neutral bathroom for students.

events.id: A Talent for Murder - British and Irish Film Festival-The Screening Room, 435 Queen St, Masterton-Event Finder
events.name: A Talent for Murder - British and Irish Film Festival
events.venue: The Screening Room, 435 Queen St, Masterton
events.long_description:
OFFICIAL SELECTION: Toronto International Film Festival -

British national treasure Helen Mirren plays The Talented Mr. Ripley author Patricia Highsmith in this deeply intriguing thriller.

A Talent for Murder takes place in 1995, with Highsmith now in her seventies - and in poor health. Retired to her secluded house in the Swiss Alps, the author keeps to her study, immersed in her books, accompanied by her cats, and surrounded by a collection of antique weapons.

Highsmith’s solitude is interrupted by the arrival of Edward Ridgeway (recent Tony-winner Alden Ehrenreich), a mysterious messenger from a New York publisher, sent to persuade the author to write one final instalment of the Ripley anthology. Aggravated by the unexpected visit from this youthful, overly eager envoy, Patricia declines the offer. That is, unless Ridgeway can help her in conjuring up the perfect murder story.

Mirren embodies the wickedly manipulative author with gusto, while Ehrenreich imbues Ridgeway with enough guile to keep us guessing at his motives.

From director Anton Corbijn (Control), A Talent for Murder is replete with brilliant twists, biting dialogue, and delicious entanglements. Direct from its world premiere at the Toronto International Film Festival, don’t miss this highly anticipated thriller!

events.long_description:
Game On, Pōneke — Women of Pōneke x Tokomanawa Queens
This one’s different.

We’re trading our usual Thursday evening for a Sunday afternoon, swapping the city for Porirua, and stepping courtside with the Tokomanawa Queens.

Women of Pōneke is heading to Te Rauparaha Arena for an afternoon of kōrero, kai, community — and live basketball. Never watched a game in your life? Great! This is your invitation!

Here’s the afternoon:

🥂 Welcome bubbles on arrival
🎤 Kōrero from Rachel Taulelei — Chair and co-owner of the Tokomanawa Queens, and one of Aotearoa’s most respected leaders in business and beyond
🍽️ Kai and time to connect
🏀 Courtside seats for Queens v Southern Hoiho — the Queens’ Inclusion Round

This is the team that made history. The Tauihi league launched with pay equity from day one, the first professional women’s sport in New Zealand to do so. The Queens won the first-ever title. And this season, they’ve welcomed WNBA talent to the roster: Charlisse Leger-Walker (the first New Zealand woman drafted to the WNBA) and her sister Krystal, alongside Hailey Van Lith, Olympic bronze medallist.

Come and join us!

Bring your people. Bring your kids — they’re welcome, with games and activities running in the Back Court and slushies and popcorn sorted. This is a whānau-friendly afternoon.

Every ticket gives back. Proceeds support Social Supermarkets in Porirua and Wellington City, fostering food security in our communities.

Tickets:
🎟️ Adult — $35
🎟️ Student — $25
🎟️ Kids — FREE

150 seats only. Once they’re gone, they’re gone.

events.id: The Fabulous Carmen Walk Tour: Tea, Toasties and Trade-Thistle Hall, 293 Cuba St, Te Aro, Wellington-Event Finder
events.name: The Fabulous Carmen Walk Tour: Tea, Toasties and Trade
events.venue: Thistle Hall, 293 Cuba St, Te Aro, Wellington
events.long_description:
Entrepreneur, entertainer, madam and mayoral candidate Carmen Rupe was based in Wellington for less than 15-years but has left us a rich legacy of memories and inspiring moments.

Join us on this free 90-minute community walk-tour as we trace Carmen's Wellington years (1967-1980). We'll visit some of the remaining inner-city business locations and imagine some of those that are no longer here: Le Balcon, Carmen's International Coffee Lounge, The Peacock, Cleopatra's Coffee Lounge, Carmen's Bazaar, The Gazebo massage parlour, The Cottage brothel and Carmen's Curio Shop.

Learn about Carmen's landmark 1966 court case, her race to become Mayor of Wellington in the 1970s, and how she supported and offered a safe harbour to Wellington's Takatāpui LGBTI Rainbow communities.

“I would more or less hypnotise all my guests like a black widow spider and trap my clients caught in my web. As people left my coffee lounge at 6am or earlier I would splash them with Carmen’s exotic juice which meant that they would be back another night for more. The scent would guide them to me. Some would hear my voice calling like an eerie whisper from the depths of darkness.” [from Carmen’s autobiography, "Carmen: My Life"]

Accessibility information: The tour is on flat public footpaths. Tours are limited to around 20 walkers.

Time/Date: 1pm, Sunday 1 November, 2026
Starts: outside Thistle Hall, 293 Cuba St, Te Aro, Wellington,
Ends: Jack Ilott Green, corner of Harris Street & Jervois Quay (just by Civic Square)
Duration: 90 minutes
Cost / Bookings: the tour is free but you do need to register

PLEASE REGISTER AT https://walktours.nz/book/

events.long_description:
Practice a VocalVinyasa class that will enliven your body. Science shows that sound vibrations, especially those from our voices, create physiological benefits that balance the body and mind.

Yoga Voice is a form of yoga combining specific vocal tones to tune into the body as a sounding and breathing apparatus. These classes are ideal for anyone who uses their voice and wants to keep their body and voice in optimal health, it can be especially beneficial for singers, actors, performers, yoga practitioners, teachers and musicians.

Cost:

Casual class $20.00

4 classes for the price of 3 $60.00 book before 1st Nov.

Student/Unwaged $10.00

Your Teacher:

Sascha Perfect (RYT 200 RYVT250)

Sascha is a qualified yoga teacher and performer. She has a RYT 200 accreditation from Hot Yoga Wellington, a RYVT 250 with Yoga Voice and is currently training to be a Soul Voice practitioner. Her yoga journey began in Ireland and she has trained with voice and somatic practitioners in Europe including Frank Van De Ven, Tadashi Endo, Enrique Pardo, Anne Marie Blink, Karina Schelde and traditional Vedic chanting with Menaka Desikachar.

events.long_description:
To celebrate the summer, we return to a much-loved Royal New Zealand Ballet production from 2011: Greg Horsman’s fairytale version of The Sleeping Beauty.
The age-old story of the princess who pricks her finger and falls into an enchanted sleep, only to be wakened by true love, is brought to life in picture-perfect designs by Gary Harris, classical choreography and Tchaikovsky’s magical music. A touch of wizardry from Wellington’s Wētā Workshop adds to the joy and wonder, making this the perfect pre-Christmas treat for audiences of all ages.

More than 42,000 people saw the premiere of this glorious production around New Zealand in 2011. Choreographer Greg Horsman left the Royal New Zealand Ballet in 2012 to take up a new role at Queensland Ballet, and this production has now been staged there several times to great acclaim.

Book more than one show from our 2026 season through our ‘Subscribe and Save’ package, and save up to 20% on your tickets

The ‘Tones of Silence’ exhibition explores through B & W photography taken with vintage camera and lenses to give another way of viewing and experiencing the Chapel. This exhibition will reveal the tones, textures, composition and forms of the Chapel in black and white with many shades of grey.

Step inside Futuna Chapel for three captivating Sunday afternoon talks covering black-and-white photography, heritage architecture, and Aotearoa New Zealand’s built history, from 2:00pm to 3:30pm during the Futuna Exhibition.

The Trust looks forward to welcoming architects, designers, graduates, students and interested members of the public to attend these events and support the Trust in its work.

The Futuna Trust is a charitable organisation and all koha received from the WHF events will go towards the ongoing care, maintenance and operation of Futuna Chapel and also to support various initiatives undertaken by the Trust. 

Please register to attend the public talks to ensure you get a seat. Seats are limited. There is no set ticket price. The gift of koha is prefered.

events.long_description:
THEME: Resetting yourself

Guided drawings to reset your wants and needs

Join us for a DRAW IT OUT drawing for wellness workshop. Practice the ‘art’ of drawing and writing for wellness. This 1.5 hour workshop takes you through guided cues (similar to meditation or journaling) to draw out where you are at, draw out how you are feeling, and draw out your own inner guidance.

We all have the resources within to guide us, this workshop creates the space to access this by using a modality called Interactive Drawing Therapy. Facilitated by Lara Phillips, this is not therapy rather drawing for wellness; a guided workshop to build one’s relationship with oneself, to strengthen self-reflection and self-care.

No drawing skills required, this is more mark making not art making.

events.long_description:
Natural Textured Rings - November Taster!
Make your own personalised ring - a gift for yourself or someone special! :-)

Learn the basic technique first in copper or brass, and then craft your final piece in silver!

Over this taster class, you’ll be guided through the process of heating and texturing metal, cutting and shaping with traditional jewellery tools. Use feathers, leaves, or fabrics to create a unique texture for a beautiful ring!

Learn to measure your finger, cut metal to length and texture it without rolling mill, hammers and punches. Then use a jewellers torch, sandpaper and polishing, and your beautiful new ring will be ready to wear.

This 3-hour class is ideal for beginners, groups of friends and visitors to the city.

Included in the class fee are copper and brass for practising on, a sterling silver ring strip and all consumables such as sandpaper, solder and chemicals. Extra metals are available for purchase in the studio.

Kids aged 12 (or so) are welcome to attend the class, but any person under the age of 16 must be accompanied by an enrolled parent or caregiver.

Workshop fee is $165, Early bird pricing $148 till 4 October.

events.long_description:
Tones of Silence; Futuna Chapel in Black & White with Catherine Hammond & John Grace
Join Catherine Hammond and John Grace for an afternoon exploring black-and-white photography, from Grace’s evocative Chapel images made with vintage cameras and 19th-century French lenses to Hammond’s insights into Aotearoa New Zealand’s early photographic history.

About the speakers

John Grace

John Grace is a commercial lawyer and amateur photographer. John’s black and white photos of Futuna Chapel have been taken on an old tripod camera using 1866 French lenses. A selection of his photos will be exhibited at the Chapel.

Catherine Hammond

"Against Forgetting: Photographic Archives in Aotearoa"

Catherine Hammond is the director of collections and research at Tāmaki Paenga Hira Auckland War Memorial Museum. She was formerly Hocken Librarian at the University of Otago Te Whare Wānanga o Ōtākou, and before that head of documentary heritage at Tāmaki Paenga Hira Auckland War Memorial Museum and research library manager at Auckland Art Gallery Toi o Tāmaki. She co-edited of ‘A Different Light/First Photography of Aotearoa’ (2024).

events.long_description:
HALLOWEEN Small Dog Social - First Sunday of the month - LATER TIME - 3:30pm-4:30pm
It's Halloween weekend so bring your dogs in their favourite costume if you want!

The Small Dog Social Walk is on the first Sunday of the month, meeting at 3:30pm during spring and summer.

The meetup will gather for free play from 3:30pm in the back half McEwan Park at Hikoikoi Reserve, Petone Beach, with the walk along the beach and back starting around 4:00pm. After the walk, feel free to hang around and let the dogs play some more.

Water bowl and poo bag bin provided!

Closest street address for GPS is 38 Marine Parade, Petone - we meet in the field across the road! There is plenty of parking along this street.

April - September - Winter time - 2:30 - 3:30
October - March - Summer time - 3:30 - 4:30

Time changes with Daylight Saving Time.

PLEASE DO NOT GATHER ON THE FRONT FIELD
On arrival, please come straight to the back field. We have had a few dogs running over to the car park in excitement to see their friends, with cars driving around we need to be very careful to keep the pooches safe at all times. If your pooch is not good off lead, please keep it on until everyone has arrived and (if you feel comfortable) then let them off.

This is open to the public, and we welcome anyone who has not been before who would like to join our amazing group of pooches and owners!
We also encourage puppies; this is the perfect place for them to socialise safely.

This group is purely a social group with no formal club functions or responsibilities. The park is also used for Disc Golf, so please watch out for people playing thru.

Anti-social small dogs are welcome. If a muzzle is needed, please ensure that they wear it.

PLEASE NOTE- Your dogs are your responsibility at all times, this includes supervising their behaviour and picking up their poop!

Feel free to post in the event or message the page if you need more info!

events.name: Celtic Caim at Greytown Upclose & Personal
events.venue: Cobblestones Heritage Village, 169 Main Street, Greytown
events.long_description:
A very special concert at Cobblestones Museum. We will welcome Celtic Caim - Heather Innes and Pauline Vallance for one concert only. Celtic Caim is a Celtic blessing and Pauline is in NZ for a short time only so we are fortunate for have secured one concert with her. Pauline and Heather, began singing together in 2014 and became Celtic Caim for tours of Canada, Australia and New Zealand in 2017, 2018 and 2019. Celtic Caim concerts have been described as "hauntingly beautiful harmony singing” and include an eclectic mix of Celtic songs, songs written by various songwriters, including Pauline & Heather plus jigs and reels on flute and bodhrán to get your feet tapping!

Pauline Vallance (vocals, clasarch, flute) is a singer/songwriter from Ayrshire, Scotland. She loves singing traditional songs from Ireland and Scotland plus her own songs, and she has a highly developed sense of the absurd! Pauline performs regularly throughout the UK. Her live performances have been described as "delightful and convivial on so many levels". Pauline’s latest album “The World's a Gift”, funded by Creative Scotland, was nominated for Scottish Album of the Year. She has written theatre shows about poets Robert Burns and Robert Tannahill as well as Echoes of the Land, which deals with having to leave your homeland and the longing for home.

Heather Innes (vocals, bodhrán) After living and singing in Australia and UK, Heather moved to New Zealand in 2022 and now lives locally in the Wairarapa. Heather sings from her heart, powerful ballads to gentle lullaby, with a timely sense of humour in between.

She began singing professionally in 1990 after recording her first album All’s Fair in Love and War at Spring Records, Rostrevor, Northern Ireland in 1989. Over the years she’s toured solo, and in bands and duos, in the UK, Australia, New Zealand, Thailand, Germany, Denmark, Ireland, Canada and USA. As well as recording 16 albums with various bands and duos, Heather has five solo CDs.

Bookings to 02102361951 by txt and $30 cash (no EFTPOS) on the door or through Eventfinda.

events.long_description:
OFFICIAL SELECTION: Toronto International Film Festival -

Oscar-nominee Saoirse Ronan delivers one of her most daring and memorable roles in the satirical thriller Bad Apples, a bold and timely film that challenges how deeply we hold our core beliefs.

Ronan plays Maria, a primary school teacher whose classroom is thrown into chaos by Danny, an exceptionally disruptive and foul-mouthed student.

Maria reaches her breaking point after Danny has a violent run-in with another student, and taking a drastic course of action, traps him in her home.

In Danny’s absence, the classroom begins to thrive; the children flourish academically, and both parents and school staff celebrate the incredible turnaround. But with everyone else convinced the school’s biggest problem has finally been solved, Maria now finds herself trapped in an increasingly preposterous moral dilemma.

Swedish-born director Jonatan Etzler injects scathing Scandi humour into this daring psychological comedy, which is sure to become one of the year’s most talked-about films.

It follows Klara, an Artificial Friend - chosen by a young girl named Josie to join her family. Emerging Waves is a space held by a 5Rhythms® Teacher in Training. In this 5Rhythms class, you are invited to move through the 5Rhythms with simple guidance, giving space for your personal expression. Music becomes the teacher alongside the Teacher in Training, supporting your movement practice through the Waves map of Flowing, Staccato, Chaos, Lyrical and Stillness.

Rooted in the teachings of Gabrielle Roth, 5Rhythms® is practiced by tens of thousands of people around the world. It is a movement meditation, a creative path, and a philosophy grounded in the belief that when we move, we heal. Movement becomes both medicine and metaphor—opening space for personal insight, and embodied presence.

This practice welcomes every body, every culture, every age, and every level of experience. Wherever the 5Rhythms are danced, a community forms—one that moves together, sweats together, grows together, and supports one another’s freedom and authenticity. Here we meet ourselves and each other with curiosity, kindness, and the courage to be real.

Creativity. Connection. Community.

Open to everyone, from complete beginners to experienced movers

events.long_description:
Experience Stonehenge Aotearoa at its most breathtaking — as the sun dips below the Wairarapa horizon.
Our Sunset Guided Tour blends astronomy, storytelling, and the natural beauty of twilight for an evening you will never forget.

Led by one of our knowledgeable guides, this 90-minute experience explores how ancient cultures used the Sun to track time and mark the turning of the seasons. You’ll discover the scientific and cultural thinking behind the Henge’s unique Southern Hemisphere design before watching the sunset alignment from inside the stone circle.

Weather permitting, you’ll witness how the setting Sun interacts with the structure — a striking moment that links ancient knowledge with the rhythms of the natural world.

Duration and Schedule
• Allow: Approximately 90 minutes
• Start Time: Begins one hour before sunset
• Availability: Offered any day with advance booking

events.name: After God
events.venue: Circa Theatre, 1 Taranaki St, Wellington
events.long_description:
From the creators of the wildly praised, fiercely original verbatim plays TRANSMISSION and TRANSMISSION:BETA, the New Zealand premiere of AFTER GOD is a theatrical journey across continents and conversations, with one of Aotearoa’s most distinguished actors, Michael Hurst, joining director Miranda Harcourt and writer Stuart McKenzie to explore big questions about meaning, madness and metaphysics.

With a hungry mind and burning questions, McKenzie hits the road — travelling from Wellington to Kathmandu, London and New York. Along the way, he encounters a vivid cast of real-life characters: theologians, Tibetan rinpoches, philosophers, cosmologists, taxi drivers, hotel receptionists, a famous singing nun — and his own mother. Each has their own radically different way of making sense of existence.

Created entirely from real conversations, AFTER GOD is a new verbatim theatre work, transforming interviews, ideas and personal stories into an exhilarating theatrical experience.

It’s a funny, provocative and hopeful exploration of what we believe, what keeps us going and what it means to be alive right now.

Re-use, Re-Purpose, Beautify with Gold!! Come along and learn the magical art of Kintsugi with Artist Ema Frost in this new Workshop.

Re-use, Re-Purpose, Beautify with Gold!!

Come along and learn the magical art of Kintsugi with Artist Ema Frost in this new Workshop. You can bring along a piece of your own pottery to restore in this beautiful style. (I'll also have a few as back up if you don't have your own piece) (All Levels)

Monday 2nd November - 9:30am - 11:30am

Kintsugi

It's called kintsugi (金継ぎ), or kintsukuroi (金繕い), literally golden (“kin”) and repair (“tsugi”). This traditional Japanese art uses a precious metal – liquid gold, liquid silver or lacquer dusted with powdered gold – to bring together the pieces of a broken pottery item and at the same time enhance the breaks.

You will take away your wonderful finished work, plus your knew skills which will enable you to further your own Kintsugi in your own time.

This class is not just for budding or accomplished artists. It is for everyone to enjoy a relaxing day of art and design with Ema.

What you will take away:

A finished artwork piece

A understanding of Kintsugi

Knowledge and History of this beautiful art form.

events.name: Mini Masterpieces - Enamels Short Course
events.venue: Workspace Studios Ōtaki, 2 Arthur Street, Ōtaki, Ōtaki
events.long_description:
Love pattern, colour and beautiful little things? You don't need to be an artist to create your own miniature masterpiece.

Glass enamels have been used on metal for centuries to create tiny works of art — from portraits and religious icons to royal emblems and intricate decorative pieces. Now it's your turn to discover this wonderfully tactile process.

Over two three-hour sessions, expert tutor Sarah Brock will guide you through creating a miniature artwork on a pre-cut metal shape. You'll start by preparing your metal and building a beautiful enamel background, then choose from a selection of patterns to trace and decals to create your design. No drawing skills are required — Sarah will help you find a design you love and show you how to make it work beautifully on your piece.

From there, you'll build up layers of coloured transparent enamels, ceramic pencil details and special effects, firing your piece between layers in the kiln. With each firing, the colours and textures develop, creating depth, richness and that gorgeous glassy enamel finish.
Your finished piece could become a special piece of jewellery, a keepsake ornament, or a tiny artwork to display in your home.

Perfect for anyone who loves colour, pattern, illustration and design, whether you're completely new to enamelling or simply looking for a new creative medium to explore. Come with an idea, or come with absolutely no idea — Sarah will help you turn it into something beautiful.
All class materials supplied.

During this course everyone will get to design and build their own awesome LED Neon Sign. The sign can be up to 50cm x 40cm and there are a range of colours available.

Only 6 Students Per Class.

Some prior soldering experience would be beneficial.

events.long_description:
Overview

Would you like to become less busy and more productive? Then our Time Management workshop is for you.

You've all heard the expression 'Time is money' Well actually time is more valuable than money because time is a non renewable resource. Do you ever have those times when you've been busy all day but feel that you have not achieved what you need to?

Effective Time Management is crucial in today's busy and competitive world. Successes and failures in work and daily activities largely depend on how time is managed. Therefore Time Management is the number one skill to master.

Do you ever feel overwhelmed by the sheer volume of work to be done? Would you like to become less busy and more productive? Then our Time Management workshop is for you. Let us show you and your organisation how to get the most out of a day with better time management skills.

WORKSHOP OBJECTIVES

Plan and prioritise each day’s activities in a more efficient and productive manner
Overcome procrastination quickly and easily
Handle crises effectively and quickly
Organise your workspace and workflow to make better use of time
Become less stressed, less busy and more productive
Delegate more efficiently
Handle interruptions and beat time wasters
Use rituals to make your life run smoother
Plan meetings more appropriately and effectively

Time management training most often begins with setting goals. These goals are recorded and may be broken down into a project, an action plan, or a simple task list. Activities are then rated based on urgency and importance, priorities assigned, and deadlines set.

This process results in a plan with a task list or calendar of activites. Routine and recurring tasks are often given less focus to free time to work on tasks that contribute to important goals. This entire process is supported by a skill set that includes personal motivation, delegation skills, organisational tools and crisis management tools.

For more information or to book: email info@biztrainers.co.nz or call 04 974 8790

events.long_description:
OFFICIAL SELECTION: Thessaloniki International Documentary Festival -

What happens when your neighbour goes completely wild? Derek vs Derek is a funny, insightful and heartwarming documentary that charts the turbulent relationship between two farmers.

On a country road in Devon live two ideologically opposed neighbouring farmers- both called Derek. Derek Banbury believes in the intensive farming of his land, while Derek Gow is focused on creating a “rewilding” oasis for nature and wildlife on his land.

Shot over three years, Derek vs Derek wonderfully juxtaposes the two wholly opposing approaches to farming, as tempers fray, wild animals run amok, and the land is radically transformed.

The two Dereks’ story will at turns amuse, entertain and provoke thought about environmental issues and the future of farming.

Award-winning director James Dawson celebrates the potential for understanding in this wonderful film about land use and farming, told by farmers. Packed to the brim with English humour, Derek vs Derek is essential viewing.

events.name: Ngā Mokopuna Tour
events.venue: Te Herenga Waka Marae, 46 Kelburn Parade, Wellington
events.long_description:
Ngā Mokopuna: A Living Building Story Tour

Join us for an introductory guided tour of Ngā Mokopuna, Te Herenga Waka Victoria University of Wellington's pioneering regenerative building project.

This experience explores the vision, values, and aspirations behind a building designed to tread lightly on the environment while creating lasting benefits for people and place. Grounded in principles of kaitiakitanga and inspired by mātauranga Māori, Ngā Mokopuna reflects a commitment to caring for our natural world and future generations.

During the tour, you'll learn about the Living Building Challenge, one of the world's most ambitious sustainability frameworks, and discover how Ngā Mokopuna has been designed to meet its rigorous standards. The project represents a significant step towards becoming one of Aotearoa New Zealand's next recognised Living Buildings.

From outside the building and surrounding precinct, you'll hear the stories behind its design, sustainability features, and cultural foundations. You'll also meet staff and student ambassadors who work and study within Ngā Mokopuna and learn firsthand how the building supports teaching, learning, wellbeing, and community.

The tour also provides an opportunity to view Te Tumu Herenga Waka Marae and hear how the marae and Ngā Mokopuna together express values of sustainability, kaitiakitanga, belonging, and connection.

Whether you're interested in sustainable design, Māori worldviews, education, architecture, or the future of the built environment, this tour offers a unique insight into a project that seeks to demonstrate what regenerative design can achieve.

Come and discover how sustainability and kaitiakitanga are being brought to life at Ngā Mokopuna.

events.long_description:
EXPLORE THE LARVAL MASK IN A SERIES OF PHYSICAL THEATRE WORKSHOPS

What can your body communicate when your face disappears?

Larval masks are oversized, simplified shapes that transform the actor into something not quite human.

Across four practical workshops, we’ll explore how larval masks can be used to develop physical character, stage presence, movement quality and non-verbal storytelling, while making space for play, curiosity and discovery.

BOOK ONE, SOME, OR ALL FOUR CLASSES

Participants can attend individual workshops or book the complete four-class series.

The full four classes are recommended, as each session builds your familiarity with the mask and gives you more opportunity to develop your physical vocabulary and apply what you've discovered to both masked and non-masked performance.

THE FOUR CLASSES

WEEK 1-TUESDAY 3rd Nov 4:30-6pm, Toi Aro

An introduction to the larval mask. Explore the relationship between mask, body and space. Begin to discover the physical language of the mask.

WEEK 2-TUESDAY 10th Nov 4:30-6pm, Toi Aro

Developing movement vocabulary through movement, rhythm, gesture and stillness. Explore a set of tools that help you communicate with your audience.

WEEK 3-TUESDAY 17th Nov 4:30-6pm, Toi Aro

The larval mask in situations. From embodying a larval character through to creating the start of simple scenes.

WEEK 4-24th Nov 4:30-6pm, Toi Aro

Putting the mask into performance. Develop short physical sequences and explore how the skills from the series can be used in performance.

WHAT YOU'LL TRAIN

Working with the larval mask will help you develop:

Physical clarity — making movement and intention readable to an audience

Presence — learning how stillness, focus and rhythm can hold attention

Economy of movement — discovering how less can communicate more

Physical character — creating a figure through the body rather than starting with psychology

Non-verbal storytelling — communicating without relying on dialogue

Play and imagination — approaching performance through curiosity rather than predetermined choices

FEE

$20 waged · $15 unwaged per workshop

Full four-class series: $70 waged · $50 unwaged

If cost is a barrier to attending, please get in touch. We may be able to help

ABOUT THE TUTOR

John Armstrong is a Wellington-based theatre-maker and educator whose practice centres on physical theatre, mask and academia.

John's physical theatre training includes residencies with Frantic Assembly in London, as well as a year of specialist mask training at Hagley Theatre School in Christchurch with Pedro Ilgenfritz. He has continually worked as an actor in professional companies, theatre-in-education programmes and as a teacher in tertiary settings. As a writer and researcher, he runs Theatre Research NZ

events.long_description:
With our November book group taking place just a few days after Halloween, we'll be discussing the classic ghost story The Turn of the Screw by Henry James. Published in 1898, it quickly became James' most popular work of short fiction.

The gothic horror novella tells of a young governess who arrives at a remote country estate to care for two children, only to become convinced that supernatural forces haunt the grounds. Even its author found it terrifying: “I had to correct the proofs of my ghost story last night,” he told poet Edmund Gosse, “and when I had finished them I was so frightened that I was afraid to go upstairs to bed!”

The group previously read Henry James' The Portrait of a Lady way back at the beginning of 2014.

Project Gutenberg link for those e-reading:
https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/209

Plus, because it's in the public domain, there are a number of audiobooks on YouTube - perhaps the perfect way to experience a ghost story...

Do you keep meaning to read more of the great classics? At Wellington Classic Literature Club, we read works that have stood the test of time, whether they were written in 1780, 1880 or even 1980. We meet on the first Tuesday of the month.

RSVP
Bookings essential. Get your free ticket by clicking 'Register' above. Limited places.

If you've signed up, but things change and you're not going to be able to make it along, please email classiclitwgtn@gmail.com as we may be able to make more spaces available for others.

VENUE
We meet in the ‘Games Room’, The Library bar's private area overlooking Courtenay Place. After you enter the bar, head to your right (up the step) and through a smaller space with booths to the large carpeted space beyond (behind the big wooden sliding door).

ABOUT US
Wellington Classic Literature Club has been running for more than a decade - since the start of 2013 - and we have a great bunch of regulars as well as readers who join us for particular books or simply when it suits.

Bhakti Lounge Wellington
Wellington, Wellington
events.long_description:
Overview

Explore dopamine, break free from everyday distractions, and find deeper fulfilment through modern psychology and timeless wisdom.

Tuesday Wellbeing Seminars:
Inspire Me!
Hooked: Navigating the Age of Dopamine




From endless scrolling and notifications to constant cravings for quick satisfaction, our minds are perpetually wired for the next hit. But why does chasing cheap dopamine leave us feeling so drained and distracted ?

​This interactive 1-hour workshop bridges modern psychology with timeless wisdom to help us break the loop.

Join us for a relaxed, interactive discussion where we explore how replacing cheap distractions with a "higher taste" can quiet the restless mind, reclaim focus, and unlock a deeper sense of fulfillment.




End the session on a high note with a delicious plant-based dinner, dessert, and good conversation.
Meet your host Sivananda

Sivananda’s background is in both science and music, holding a Master's Degree in Data Science, a Bachelor of Science in Physics and a long history of playing and performing on the double bass. His passion for philosophy, music, good food and community attracted him to the bhakti lifestyle. Having studied and practiced the science of the ‘self’ for six years now, he thrives on drawing insights from contemporary science and combining it with yoga wisdom to encourage others to explore new perspectives.

events.id: RNZB – Costume in Motion-St James Theatre, 77-87 Courtenay Place, Wellington-Event Finder
events.name: RNZB – Costume in Motion
events.venue: St James Theatre, 77-87 Courtenay Place, Wellington
events.long_description:
Join the RNZB Foundation and the Royal New Zealand Ballet for a very special fundraising event at Wellington’s St James Theatre, celebrating the artistry, history and craftsmanship of ballet costume.

Guests will enjoy a rare opportunity to see treasured costumes from the RNZB collection up close, including pieces seldom seen outside performance. Discover the extraordinary detail, skill and workmanship behind these magnificent creations, and hear the stories of the designers, craftspeople, dancers and productions they were made for.

The evening will feature a runway presentation, with RNZB dancers modelling selected costumes from ballets across the company’s history. Afterwards, meet and mingle with the dancers in costume, and speak with some of the RNZB costumiers who help bring these works of art to life.

With live music, drinks and canapés included, this unique evening also supports the RNZB Foundation, with part of each ticket price received as a donation.

Donation receipt will be issued by the Royal New Zealand Ballet

This event is possible with the generous support of Venues Wellington and the Royal New Zealand Ballet.

events.id: Read NZ Te Pou Muramura annual pānui with David Hill-70 Molesworth Street, Thorndon, Wellington 6011, New Zealand-Humanitix
events.name: Read NZ Te Pou Muramura annual pānui with David Hill
events.venue: 70 Molesworth Street, Thorndon, Wellington 6011, New Zealand
events.long_description:
“One of my friends regularly asks ‘'What are you reading at the moment?’' He assumes that I am reading, and will always continue to do so. I have the same assumption.”

Join lit legend David Hill as he explores what it means to read, who’s doing it, and why on earth anyone isn’t.

 

In this one-time only public lecture at the National Library of New Zealand in Te Whanganui-a-Tara, David will share his thoughts on reading as a pathway to compassion, self-reflection and happiness—all with the characteristic David Hill warmth and wit.

With an introduction from journalist and award-winning author Claire Mabey, the Read NZ Te Pou Muramura Pānui is a public lecture held at the National Library of New Zealand followed by a printed edition available in a small booklet. Current paid Read NZ members will receive a booklet free on the night, for others it’s available to purchase.

For teachers who use his books in class, this is an invaluable behind-the-scenes insight into the mind of one of Aotearoa NZ’s most celebrated storytellers.

 

For David’s fans, peers, and all literary afficionados—this event is not to be missed.

 

Entry is free, but RSVPing via Humanitix is essential to secure your seat.

 

#

 

Read NZ Te Pou Muramura is a registered charity and the annual Pānui is an opportunity for a leader within the literary sphere to reflect and share their thoughts on reading and writing.

Entry is free

Te Puna Mātaruanga o Aotearoa Auditorium at the National Library of New Zealand

Bookings through Humanitix are essential

Join us for celebratory drinks and nibbles in the foyer afterwards

Printed copies of the Read NZ Te Pou Muramura David Hill Pānui will be provided to current individual members, with copies also available to purchase

events.name: A Painful Story: Album Cinema Showing
events.venue: Wallace Street, Mount Cook, Wellington 6021, New Zealand
events.long_description:
Sam Podmore is a young Zimbabwean Pop and Electronic artist and producer whose relationship with music began in an unexpected place, sitting at an old grand piano on a family holiday. Now, four years later, his debut album, A Painful Story, is an intimate exploration of loss, homesickness and the search for peace amidst the complexities of cultural change.

Moving between Afro, EDM, hip hop and analogue pop, Sam invites listeners into a story that is deeply his own while remaining relatable in its themes of belonging, change and connection. A Painful Story is ultimately an exploration of what we carry with us, what we leave behind, and how we learn to make peace with the places and people that shape us.

This exclusive showing of A Painful Story, music, visuals and all is the first time the world gets to see the creativity, hard work and production mastery on display, in a one-off pre-release showing that you don't want to miss.

Tickets will go fast....

events.id: Who was Dr Leonard Cockayne?-Tāne Whakapiripiri - Ōtari Visitors Centre, 150 Wilton Road, Wilton, Wellington, Wellington-Event Finder
events.name: Who was Dr Leonard Cockayne?
events.venue: Tāne Whakapiripiri - Ōtari Visitors Centre, 150 Wilton Road, Wilton, Wellington, Wellington
events.long_description:
We all know of Dr Cockayne’s work here at Ōtari, but he did so much more. Cockayne was a prolific writer of botanical and scientific reports and helped to secure the protection of significant conservation areas around New Zealand. This, centenary year is surely a good time to find out more about Dr Cockayne from Trustees Dr Carol West and Kathy Ombler.

Located in Tāne Whakapiripiri, Ōtari Visitor Centre. Gold coin donation. No need to book, just turn up!

This seminar is part of the Ōtari-Wilton’s Bush Trust’s annual seminar series. This year, they are on the first Tuesday of the month, March – November, to celebrate 100 years of Ōtari-Wilton’s Bush.

Ōtari 100: Celebrating 100 years of native plants, conservation, and community. 1926-2026.

events.venue: Willis Street Village, 5 / 148 Willis Street, New Zealand 6011,148 Willis St, Te Aro, Wellington 6011, New Zealand, Wellington
events.long_description:
Vincents Annual Group Exhibition - Opening Night
Vincents Art Workshop presents

Annual Group Exhibition 2026

4 – 30 November
Vincents Gallery
Willis St Village, 5/148 Willis St
Opening night: Wednesday 4th November, 5:30pm–7:00pm

Nau mai, haere mai! Vincents Art Workshop warmly invites you to the opening of its Annual Group Exhibition 2026. Following the success of last year’s 40th Anniversary Exhibition at Tākina, this year’s celebration returns home to Vincents Gallery in the heart of Wellington’s CBD.
Step inside and discover a vibrant showcase of work by the talented artists who attend our inclusive community art studio—a welcoming space where people from all walks of life create side by side. The exhibition celebrates the remarkable breadth of creativity within our studio, with painting, printmaking, ceramics, woodcraft, fabric art, and many other craft media on display.
Come along, meet the artists, celebrate their creativity, and support a much-loved part of Wellington’s arts community. With an exciting range of original works to explore, you may even discover the perfect piece to take home or give as a special gift.

Vincents Gallery exhibitions are supported by Wellington City Council’s Annual Stability Fund.

Vincents Art Workshop
Art Changing Lives since 1985

Press enquiries:
Andrew Mitchell
Coordinator / Kaiwhakahaere
Email:
Phone: 04 4991030

events.id: Café Scientifiqué: Super El Niño-Southern Cross - Garden Bar & Restaurant, 39 Abel Smith St, Te Aro, Wellington-Event Finder
events.name: Café Scientifiqué: Super El Niño
events.venue: Southern Cross - Garden Bar & Restaurant, 39 Abel Smith St, Te Aro, Wellington
events.long_description:
Join two leading climate scientists bringing perspectives from atmospheric science and oceanography as they explore what a Super El Niño is, and what it could mean for Aotearoa New Zealand.

After brief 10–15 minute opening talks, we’ll pause for drinks before moving into an extended Q&A and kōrero. This is a conversation-led session, with lots of time for your questions and discussion.

Doors open at 5.30 pm, talks begin at 5.45 pm. All welcome—free entry, nibbles provided

Speakers

Professor James Renwick

James is a Professor of Physical Geography at Te Herenga Waka—Victoria University of Wellington, with a background in atmospheric physics, mathematics, and statistics. He has an interest in many aspects of climate, from the distant past to the near future, with a particular interest in New Zealand's climate.

Professor Craig Stevens

Craig is a Principal Scientist in Marine Physics at Earth Sciences NZ and Professor of Physics at the University of Auckland. His research explores how the ocean stores heat and the influence on the climate system. He has a focus on how to measure this heat content in some of the least observed parts of the ocean.

What is Café Scientifique?

Café Scientifique is a place where anyone can come to explore the latest ideas in science and technology in a relaxed, friendly environment. Each event begind with a short introduction from the speakers, followed by a question-and-answer conversation.

Please note: anyone under the age of 18 must be accompanied by a parent or legal guardian.

Café Scientifique is hosted by Pūtaiao ki te Pāpori—School of Science in Society. For further information, please contact scienceinsociety@vuw.ac.nz.

events.id: "From Tawa to Oxford” An evening with Sir Ashley Bloomfield-1 Lyndhurst Road, Tawa, Wellington 5028, New Zealand-Humanitix
events.name: "From Tawa to Oxford” An evening with Sir Ashley Bloomfield
events.venue: 1 Lyndhurst Road, Tawa, Wellington 5028, New Zealand
events.long_description:
Leading self and others through unique and uncertain times

Join us for a special evening with Professor Sir Ashley Bloomfield as he returns to Tawa to share stories, reflections, and leadership lessons from his life and career.

From his connections with the Tawa community to leading New Zealand through the extraordinary uncertainty of the COVID-19 pandemic, Sir Ashley will offer a fascinating and personal look at the experiences that shaped him, the lessons he learned about leadership, trust and communication, and why strong communities matter when times get tough.

During the evening, Sir Ashley will share:

His personal connections with Tawa and what the community meant to him growing up, including his family's connections with Tawa Baptist and Tawa Anglican churches.

What it was really like leading through the COVID-19 pandemic - navigating enormous pressure and uncertainty, including more than 300 of those now-famous 1pm briefings.

Why trust and communication matter - particularly when the pressure is high and people are looking to you for clarity and direction.

What the pandemic taught us about community - and the importance of looking out for one another during difficult and uncertain times.

The experiences that shaped his approach to leadership - from training as a Territorial Infantry Officer to some memorable adventures hitchhiking around New Zealand.

Whether you're interested in leadership, community, New Zealand's recent history, or simply curious to hear the stories behind one of the country's most recognisable public figures, this promises to be a fascinating and memorable evening.

An Evening With a Purpose

From Tawa to Oxford is a fundraising event supporting the redevelopment of Tawa Anglican Church.

The redevelopment will create a welcoming facility designed to serve both the church and the wider community, with spaces for community groups, meetings, workshops, support services, events, and connection.

Proceeds from ticket sales will go towards the redevelopment project, so your ticket isn't just your entry to a special evening. It's also a contribution towards creating a community space that will serve Tawa for years to come.

Event Details

Wednesday, 4 November 2026

6:30pm

Emmaus Centre

Tickets: $50

Dessert & coffee provided

Come and hear the stories behind the public figure, discover the experiences that shaped his leadership, and enjoy a thought-provoking evening about navigating uncertainty, building trust, and the power of community.

Book your ticket and join us for From Tawa to Oxford: An Evening with Sir Ashley Bloomfield.

events.id: The Racket Lounge-Bedlam and Squalor, Upstairs, 18 Garrett Street, Te Aro, Wellington-Event Finder
events.name: The Racket Lounge
events.venue: Bedlam and Squalor, Upstairs, 18 Garrett Street, Te Aro, Wellington
events.long_description:
Grab a spot on our couch and enjoy the noise at The Racket Lounge - a chill classical music series showcasing up-and-coming Pōneke musicians.

If you’ve never been to a classical concert before, or if you have and now you want to see talented emerging musicians experimenting and playing what they want to play, then The Racket Lounge is for you. Over the past two seasons we’ve seen classical covers, jazz ensembles, video game soundtracks, original compositions, loop pedals, poetry and much more. Our 2026 season is shaping up to be just as epic, plus with your tickets starting at just $5 you can afford to take a chance on something new.

Each concert will feature a different line up of musicians and genres, to be announced a week before each session. If you’re a musician looking to perform at The Racket Lounge, then head to the New Zealand String Quartet’s website to see how to apply.

We are so ready to be entranced by Wellington’s top up-and-coming talent at our second Racket Lounge session, “Moonlight Dash”. Filled with cozy, romantic grooves from 1836 to 2026, these stunningly talented up and comers are set to dazzle us whether the moon is shining bright or we’re dashing through the rain. Sip your drink through soulful, acoustic moments and tap your toes to inspiringly energetic rhythms. Come inside and soak up the chillest of vibes (rather than Wellington’s very chilly rain) at The Racket Lounge: Moonlight Dash. 

The Racket Lounge is created and presented by the New Zealand String Quartet Trust - Te Rōpū Tūrū o Aotearoa, New Zealand’s longest-running professional string quartet. With support from Wellington City Council.

Our ticket prices range from $5 to $100, so just pick the ticket price you feel like paying. At The Racket Lounge, we believe everyone should have access to high-quality but affordable art. If you're a bit strapped for cash right now, but still want a good night out, no worries! Just book yourself a $5 ticket! If you can afford to pay a little more and want to do some good for your community, then pick one of our higher ticket prices and rest assured that your dollars are going towards funding great, accessible art in your city.

All proceeds from ticket sales will go directly into presenting the next Racket Lounge, including paying musicians and artists, hiring instruments and marketing costs. Plus, by choosing a higher price point, you're ensuring that we're able to continue to offer tickets at a lower price point for those who need it.

PLEASE NOTE: Bedlam & Squalor is a licensed venue, so under 18s must be accompanied by a parent or legal guardian. Everyone must bring ID.

events.long_description:
Home Brew's legendary 'Last Week' EP has come of age and it's coming to the capital to celebrate. Released 18 years ago, 'Last Week' follows seven days in the life of roguish hip-hop crew Home Brew.
The group built a devoted following through a string of independent releases in the early 2010s. Its self-titled debut album in 2012 reached number one in New Zealand. The group returned to the charts in 2023 with 'Run It Back', introducing its music to a new generation of listeners.
The group will play 'Last Week' in full at Shed 6, alongside favourites from its celebrated catalogue. Known for a DIY approach and uncompromising sound, Home Brew remains one of the country's most celebrated hip-hop acts. The show offers Wellington fans the chance to revisit a landmark release and hear the songs that have shaped the group's enduring legacy.

events.name: 2026 EMPA Conference New Zealand
events.venue: Tākina Wellington Convention Centre, 50 Cable Street, Te Aro, Wellington, Wellington
events.long_description:
Hosted once again at Wellington’s Te Papa on Thursday 5th and Friday 6th November, the EMPA NZ conference committee has pulled together another outstanding programme of presentations, workshops and networking.

One of this year’s international speakers will be Mark Ryan, who is the General Manager of Disaster and Emergency Management and Local Disaster Coordinator for the City of Gold Coast and will be sharing lessons learned from Cyclone Alfred. Mark’s presentation was one of the highlights of the recent EMPA conference in Brisbane and we’re delighted he has accepted our invitation to pop over the Tasman in November.

Lucy Easthope is an international expert and adviser on emergency planning and disaster recovery, who will be speaking about her experiences from mass casualty events. She is a visiting professor in mass fatalities and pandemics at the Centre for Death and Society at the University of Bath and also a researcher at the Joint Centre for Disaster Research at Massey University here in New Zealand.

Closer to home, Judge Anna Tutton will be providing us with an introduction to coronial inquests following an emergency and we’ll also hear from some of those emergency communicators who have been called to give evidence.

Jo Lynskey, Emergency Management Officer and Recovery Manager for the Western Bay of Plenty District Council, will also be presenting a case study on the recovery from recent landslides and flooding in the region.

The full programme can be found at https://www.empa.org.au/

The conference also features the finalists from our annual Awards for Excellence in Emergency Communication with six different categories covering all aspects of communicating in emergency situations.

We look forward to celebrating the very best projects from the last 12 months in style at our gala awards dinner on the Thursday evening.

The Chapel of Our Lady of Compassion Tour
Join a tour of our Category 1 Historic Place Chapel and Resting Place of Meri Hōhepa Suzanne Aubert. Come experience the rich history of this sacred space.

Two forty-five-minute tours will be offered over the course of each morning. Each tour will include the history of the building, the meanings behind the stained-glass windows, and the significance of the site as an ongoing place of worship. Participants will have the opportunity to visit the final Resting Place of Meri Hōhepa Suzanne Aubert who founded the Sisters of Compassion, the only religious order born in Aotearoa New Zealand. Come and experience the rich history and spirituality that are embedded in these sacred places.

Our Cloister Cafe will be open to welcome you for coffee or lunch. Please stick around after your tour and enjoy the cafe and grounds!

Booking is REQUIRED for this event.

events.venue: The Screening Room, 435 Queen St, Masterton
events.long_description:
OFFICIAL SELECTION: Edinburgh International Film Festival -

This enchanting adaptation of Jay Parini’s semi-fictional memoir is filled with warmth, wit, and beautiful scenery from the Scottish countryside.

As a young doctoral student in the 1970s, Parini (Fionn Whitehead, Dunkirk) was somehow partnered on a road trip through the Scottish Highlands with the literary icon Jorge Luis Borges (Luis Gnecco).

Parini is both bewildered and enchanted by his eccentric companion, the blind poet’s presence leading to amusing and even poignant adventures. Over the course of an eventful journey, the two forge a deep connection, woven with poetry, music, and a touch of melancholy.

Borges and Me revels in the splendour of its locations. Gorgeously photographed, the raw beauty of the rural Scottish landscape translates beautifully to the big screen.

Whitehead and Gnecco are superb as the central pair, with a terrific supporting cast including Alan Cumming, Peter Mullan and Freya Mavor. Pack your bags, this is a road trip you can’t afford to miss.

events.long_description:
Wellington Heritage Festival: Matangireia - A Place for Māori at Parliament
Join Parliamentary Service with an insightful look at the history and stories of our historic Māori Affairs Committee Room - Matangireia.

Hear from Ellen Andersen, Director Kaiwhakahaere Tautiaki Taonga me Kaupapa Māori at Heritage New Zealand, about how Matangireia came about as a "place for Māori at Parliament" over a century ago, and how the stories and role of the room have evolved over time. In 2022, a large-scale conservation project of the room was undertaken to commemorate 100 years since the opening of the room, so this event will also give attendees an insight into how heritage is preserved over time, and what is involved in ensuring historic spaces can remain cared for and in use for the future.

Booking is REQUIRED for this event.

events.id: Botanical Insights Talk - Electrical Secrets of Plants and Fungi-Wellington Botanic Garden, 101 Glenmore St, Kelburn, Wellington-Event Finder
events.name: Botanical Insights Talk - Electrical Secrets of Plants and Fungi
events.venue: Wellington Botanic Garden, 101 Glenmore St, Kelburn, Wellington
events.long_description:
This one-hour talk will reveal how plants’ electrical signalling system enables them to sense and respond rapidly, within seconds, to their environment in order to coordinate growth, defence, photosynthesis and whole of-plant acclimation. It will outline the practical application of research findings. The talk will also examine electrical signalling in fungi and the actions of their mycelial networks in a range of biological and environmental settings. It will touch on the emergent field of fungal computers and probable applications

Located in the Seminar Room, Treehouse Visitor Centre and Shop, Wellington Botanic Garden ki Paekākā.
Free of charge. You’re welcome to bring along your own ‘brown bag’ lunch to enjoy during the talk.

The speaker is Reg Harris, a volunteer guide [botany] at Wellington Botanic Garden.
Reg delivers botany lectures for diverse audiences, delving into plant interactions, adaptive radiation, tropisms, and more. As a dedicated volunteer guide at Wellington Botanic Garden (WBG), he pioneered collaborations between WBG and Victoria University, organising annual field labs for biology students.

events.venue: 5 Park Road, Miramar, Wellington 6022, New Zealand
events.long_description:
Join us for a community screening of The Way of the Raukura, an award-winning documentary exploring the story of Parihaka and the enduring legacy of peaceful resistance led by Te Whiti o Rongomai and Tohu Kākahi.

Parihaka remains one of the most significant stories in the history of Aotearoa New Zealand. Through powerful storytelling, the film invites audiences to reflect on leadership, courage, justice and community resilience, and the lessons that continue to resonate today.

The screening provides an opportunity for Wellingtonians to learn more about this important history and its connections to our city. The evening will include a pre-film kōrero from Parihaka uri to provide historical context.

Nau mai, haere mai.

events.long_description:
Fundraiser Quiz Night

Join us for a fun night of trivia, laughs, food, drinks and prizes - all while supporting the NCWNZ Wellington Branch and Conversations with Wāhine radio show and podcast.

This fundraiser will help support the continued production of Conversations with Wāhine, a fully volunteer-led podcast and Wellington Access Radio show.

Event Details

Thursday 5 November 2026

Press Hall
80 Willis Street, Wellington Central, Wellington 6011

Doors open: 5:30pm
Quiz starts: 6:00pm

Tickets

There are several ways to take part:

• Team of 6 – $80
• Team of 7 – $90
• Team of 8 – $100
• Individual ticket – $15 per person

Coming on your own? No problem! We’ll put individual attendees into teams on arrival.

If you are booking as a team, one person can purchase the team ticket on behalf of the group.

Teams will only be registered once payment has been received. Please follow the payment instructions provided when booking and use the your name as the reference so we can match your payment to your booking.

On the Night

Each table will receive one free bowl of fries.

Food and drinks will also be available to purchase from the bar throughout the evening.

Got a tricky question? You can purchase answers throughout the quiz for $2 each!

There will also be a raffle drawn at the end of the evening:

• $2 per ticket
• 3 tickets for $5

Prizes will be announced soon!

Your Quizmaster

We’re excited to have Wellington comedian Katy Borrows as our quizmaster for the evening.

Katy is a Wellington-based comedian who has performed across New Zealand and emerged as a finalist in Wellington’s Raw Comedy Quest.

Come along, bring your friends, test your general knowledge and support Conversations with Wāhine, a fully volunteer-led podcast and Wellington Access Radio show!

We look forward to seeing you there!

Supporting

Conversations with Wāhine, podcast and radio show, part of the Wellington Branch of the National Council of Women of New Zealand.
