events.long_description:
WELCOME SPACE BROTHERS is a documentary that dives into the extraordinary true story of the Unarius Academy of Science, an extraterrestrial-channeling spiritual school founded in El Cajon in the 1970s. Led by the dazzlingly outlandish Ruth E. Norman—revered as "Archangel Uriel"—Unarius evolved into a wildly inventive public-access television phenomenon. The group produced films that appeared to be elaborately campy space epics yet were, at their core, sincere therapeutic works. 

From The Source Family director Jodi Wille comes another mind-expanding voyage into the wild frontiers of American belief, bringing her singular blend of empathy, humor, and emotional insight to one of the country's most fascinating outsider communities. Produced by Caryn Capotosto (Won’t You Be My Neighbor) and Jodi Wille. Executive producers include Elijah Wood, Moby, and Oscar-winning filmmakers Phil Lord and Christopher Miller.

Please join us for the Wellington screening of WELCOME SPACE BROTHERS - brought to you by Erika Grant and Night Church Cinema. This is a dress up event - come dressed in your favorite UFO/Cult fit. There will be prizes for best dressed, and DJ's Oona Verse and Martyn Pepperell plus others will guide us into the wild starry night with space cult inspired dance tracks.

The bar and restaurant will be open for dinner and drinks. This is a one off event, not to be missed!!

“Wild and Very Trippy” - Jodi Wille

“If I didn’t know Jodi Wille’s film, Welcome Space Brothers, was a documentary, I’d swear it was a WTF, insane, sci-fi tale of weirdness. The story of Ruth is fascinating…..” - Alan NG, Film Threat 

“It’s a vision of healing, acceptance, peace, cooperation, and hope, expressed through an outpouring of unbridled creative energy. If that spells crazy, beam me up!” — Doug Harvey, Artillery

events.venue: Plimmerton Railway Station,Plimmerton, New Zealand, Porirua
events.long_description:
Raurimu Thunder
Mainline Steam Heritage Trust is embarking on our biggest trip of the year. Modern diesel trains cover this route daily without a second thought, but we are doing something entirely different. We are throwing out the modern dampening, bypassing the mundane, and tackling New Zealand's greatest rail challenge the way it was meant to be conquered: with raw, untamed steam power.

Raurimu Thunder puts you trackside and onboard as our heavy heritage steam locomotive charges into the rugged heart of the North Island to take on the legendary Raurimu Spiral. This is a full day, high horsepower assault on a brutal mountain grade. No filters, no computer assists—just pure, unfiltered vintage engineering working at the absolute limit.

Relax in climate controlled comfort or head to the open air viewing platform to hear and see our heritage steam locomotive charge across dramatic landscapes and tackle the country's most legendary railway challenge. Large panoramic windows frame the unfolding wilderness, ensuring you enjoy every moment of the giant climb in absolute comfort, no matter the unpredictable Central Plateau weather.

How Your Day Flows:
The Scenic Approach: Settle into our premium carriages at your local station as the whistle blows and the journey begins. We steam smoothly through rolling rural valleys toward the base of the Central Plateau. Indulge in fresh barista coffee, artisan snacks, or a local craft beer from the fully stocked cafe carriage as the excitement builds.

Conquering the Spiral: Feel the earth shake as our locomotive battles the 1 in 50 grade of the world famous Raurimu Spiral. This 1898 engineering masterpiece overcomes a massive 139 metre vertical rise through a brilliant layout of horseshoe curves, deep tunnels, and a complete 360 degree loop. Experience the tight, coiling geometry firsthand from the outdoor platform, where you can practically see the front of the train loop right over the back.

The Trackside Photo Runby: Step off the train directly onto the rugged track ballast for the ultimate adventure highlight. Clear your camera lenses and find your vantage point along the tracks. Feel the anticipation build as the massive steam locomotive sets back out of sight, then marvel at the raw power as it charges back up the spiral for an unforgettable, full steam display.

The Atmospheric Return: Board your assigned premium carriage at the summit for a cozy, relaxing journey home. Swap stories with fellow travellers and enjoy a premium glass of regional wine from the salon bar as the train rolls comfortably into the night, concluding an epic day of New Zealand rail history.

Silver Star Dinner Service

As the day draws to a close and the train settles into its evening journey home, make the most of the experience with our Silver Star Dinner Service.

For $26.99 per meal, enjoy a freshly prepared dinner from Hungry Rush Ohakune, served during the return journey. It’s the perfect way to relax after a day of steam, scenery and adventure.

Choose your preferred dinner option when you book, with your selection made and paid for conveniently during checkout.

Your Dinner Choices:

The Wingman
Tender smoked chicken wings, marinated in chipotle buttermilk and served with crispy fries and a smoky hickory cola BBQ sauce.

The Burger & Fries
A juicy New Zealand beef burger with American cheese, grilled onions, pickles and house burger sauce, served in a fresh milk bun with crispy fries.

Fish & Chips
Fresh East Coast tarakihi in a light, crispy batter, served with golden fries, minted peas, fresh lemon and a house-made dipping sauce.

The No Meat Burger & Fries — Vegetarian
A delicious vegetarian burger featuring a seasoned vegetable patty with Swiss cheese, grilled onions, seasonal sauce and vegetable pickles, served in a fresh milk bun with crispy fries.

The Silver Star Dinner Service is completely optional and is not included in the standard ticket price. Dinner can be added to your booking during checkout for $26.99 per meal.

The Old Mill Track is an up and back route that runs from the Haurangi Road end to the west branch headwaters of the Tūranganui River (return).
It is approximately 4km one way (8km return), and follows a recently maintained tramping track that runs through regenerating native forest in the Aorangi Forest Park.

Transport will be provided by bus from the Martinborough town square to the Department of Conservation's Waikuku Lodge, where the walk will begin. (No access to Lodge)
Walkers will be delivered back to Martinborough town square at the end of the day.

This walk is suitable for fit trampers, with approximately 4 hours of tramping with the terrain including moderate hills to climb both up and down.

events.name: Kuratawhiti Heritage Loop
events.venue: Greytown, Kuratawhiti Street, Greytown
events.long_description:
Kuratawhiti Street stretches between urban and rural settings and this guided walk will pause briefly at the boundaries at a number of significant buildings.
The walk skirts churches, parks, memorials and settler houses. Volunteers from the Greytown Heritage Trust will share histories and insights along the way.
At midpoint in the walk we will pause for coffee and pastries at Stable - a cafe set in a countryside garden. The last stretch of the walk is entirely rural, briefly touches the Waiohine and returns by a walking track formed from an unmade road. Against a backdrop of the distant Tararuas, we face expansive views across a farming landscape towards the eastern hills.

Participants will need sturdy walk shoes or sneakers with good tread.

The ticket price for this event includes a $10 donation to the Greytown Heritage Trust to develop their digital guide and $20 for a fabulous morning tea at Stable Cafe.

events.id: One Day Secular Meditation Retreat in Wellington-31 Lawson Place, Mount Victoria, Wellington 6011, New Zealand-Humanitix
events.name: One Day Secular Meditation Retreat in Wellington
events.venue: 31 Lawson Place, Mount Victoria, Wellington 6011, New Zealand
events.long_description:
We know from ancient wisdom and modern psychology that meditation brings many benefits for our mental and physical wellbeing. It can reduce worry and pain, and improve calmness, focus, sleep, relationships and life satisfaction. The more time we spend meditating, and the more skilled we become, the greater the benefits.

So take a restorative break from your daily life, meet other meditators, and strengthen your practice at this small-group Sunday retreat. Everyone is welcome, whatever their level of meditation experience or preferred style. The retreat is beginner-friendly, and our approach is secular (meaning non-religious) which makes room for diverse beliefs.

The programme

We will begin with introductions, followed by a guided meditation that covers the core skills of both sitting and walking meditation. For the rest of the day, the meditation will be unguided apart from occasional bells to announce breaks, and to remind you to alternate between sitting and walking (if that's what you choose to do).

To help quieten the mind, many participants prefer not to talk again until the discussion circle at the end of the retreat. However some people like to chat with others during the breaks, and there is space allocated for this. The retreat leaders are always available for quiet conversations if you need support with your practice.

The venue

The Innermost Gardens hall is nestled between the central city suburb of Mount Victoria and the green town belt. This provides a peaceful nature-rich setting for the retreat, surrounded by community gardens to enjoy during the breaks or walking meditation.

There will be hot drinks and snacks available throughout the day. For lunch the participants bring a plate of vegetarian food to share. The venue has a full kitchen including cutlery, plates, bowls, fridge, stove, and a microwave.

The leaders

Bryan Royds is an adult educator and registered counsellor with a passion for wellbeing science and leadership development. He has been meditating and teaching meditation skills in groups for many years, including the well-researched methods of Mindfulness Based Stress Reduction (MBSR).

Sarah Jane Barnett is a writer and creative writing teacher at Massey University. She has been a Buddhist for ten years, practicing mostly Vipassana meditation. She also co-facilitates a meditation group for people who practice Acceptance and Commitment Therapy (an evidence-based modern psychotherapy and wellbeing method).

The registration fee is only $40 for waged and $20 for unwaged, fully refundable until one day prior.

Cheesemaking - Farmhouse Cheddar Cheese Workshop
During this hands-on workshop, you’ll be guided through each step of the cheesemaking process while making your very own round of farmhouse style cheddar.
The fee includes a cheese press (value $95.00) which can be used every time you want to make a hard cheese. It holds up to 6 litres of milk and this is what you’ll be taking your cheese home in to press for 12 hours after the workshop. All ingredients, recipes and a full set of course notes are provided.
You’ll also receive comprehensive instruction on how to wax (if you choose to) and then mature your cheese over the next five weeks. Alexis will also demonstrate how to make halloumi cheese which will then be grilled for you to enjoy! There’ll be a short lunch break and cheese making supplies such as wax will be available to purchase.

• Describe the basics of sanitisation and hygiene
• Recognise the difference between raw and pasteurised milk and know where to source them

events.name: Get the Job: STARR Interview Technique And Preparation
events.venue: Wellington High School, 249 Taranaki St, Wellington
events.long_description:
Get the best results in job interviews. Learn how to approach behavioural questions and impress the interview panel. Ace interviews using the potent Starr method. Use it to your advantage by answering competency focused questions with winning replies.

Meet the demand for excellence in the job market head on. Learn how to utilise the Starr technique in the way that recruiters use it. That is, to define and seek out the skills and qualities of the best candidate. Master the Starr skills and feel confident in your next job interview.

Familarise yourself with the skills needed to ace your next interview. Learn the STARR method as an approach to responding to behavioural based questions. Understand how to use concrete examples from your life as proof that you possess the experience and skills for the job you are applying for. You’ll develop the key interview skill of being able to share your accomplishments through real-life examples.

In this course, you are taught how to identify specific example situations that are unique to you. You’ll learn how to confidently talk about the tasks involved and describe how you completed the key task and met its challenges. We’ll also consider the context of jobs you are interviewing for and how to choose examples that best show the desired skills interviewers are seeking.

events.long_description:
This course is free for NZ citizens and residents.  Please enrol online and bring photo ID when attending the workshop.

If you are not a NZ citizen or resident, a fee of $120 applies and you must phone the office on 04 385 8919 to register.

Together, workshop participants will demystify how artificial intelligence actually works, acknowledge some of the harms of this new technology, learn about the characteristics of mis/disinformation, build resilience against fake news, and explore why our brains weren’t built for the infinite scroll. You will walk away from the workshop with a better understanding of the hidden forces shaping your screen, equipped with real-world tools to cut through the digital noise.
 
Dr. Andrew Chen is a leading New Zealand specialist at the intersection of digital technology ethics and public policy. With a PhD from the University of Auckland in Computer Systems Engineering, Andrew brings a deep technical understanding and applies it towards systemic issues and interventions. With extensive experience advising public agencies and private companies on governing emerging technologies, Dr. Chen translates complex technical concepts into clear, accessible insights for the community. He is passionate about helping people understand technology's societal impacts, and thinking more deeply about what’s happening behind the scenes, so we can all navigate today’s complex digital landscape.

events.long_description:
Tour this historically significant complex, built during World War I to provide recreation and hospitality for soldiers training at Featherston Military Camp.

Enjoy a fascinating guided tour of the historically significant Anzac Hall. The hall was first opened in 1916 as a recreation centre for the troops at the nearby Featherston military camp, with the families of the first European settlers donating the funds. events.id: Botanical Blues - Photographic cyanotype-Inverlochy Art School, 3 Inverlochy Place, Wellington-Event Finder
events.name: Botanical Blues - Photographic cyanotype
events.venue: Inverlochy Art School, 3 Inverlochy Place, Wellington
events.long_description:
In this workshop, you’ll discover the beautiful 19th-century photographic process of the cyanotype (often called a blueprint), known for its striking Prussian blue tones. In its earliest form, the cyanotype was used to record botanical specimens.

During our workshop, you’ll collect plants or foliage from the garden (or bring your own) to create delicate contact prints, OR you can create stencils for abstract designs. We’ll coat Japanese rice paper with light-sensitive chemistry, expose your designs in the sunlight, and develop them. We’ll also cut a matt board for your favourite final print. You can bring your own papers to test printing on, but they must be non-coated (able to absorb chemistry) and wet-strength.

All materials included.

Thirty minute lunch - bring a packed lunch to have in our historic home or explore the local cafes in Te Aro.

Discover the beauty of Hāpua Farm, a property that combines rolling farmland with wetlands, native bush, and sweeping views of the surrounding hill country.
Led by Michael Birch, the walk begins on the farm’s airstrip, offering beautiful views of the Tararua Ranges before descending through farm tracks, open paddocks, and bush trails.

Along the way, explore wetlands created by large landslides 11,000–12,000 years ago, and continue east to two protected QEII covenant areas of native bush.
Here, you’ll encounter towering totara, matai, and kahikatea, as well as abundant birdlife including kererū and tūī.
Last year's participants had rave reviews of this walk!

Note: the terrain is a mixture of moderate and steep hills, including rough ground and bush tracks. You will need to climb over fences using stiles.

Join us to celebrate a very big building's very big birthday!

Old Government Buildings turns 150 this year. Opened in 1876, Pōneke's most eye-catching Neo-Renaissance icon is one of the world's largest wooden buildings. Once home to the entire Wellington-based civil service, today the building houses Te Herenga Waka Victoria University's Faculty of Law, and is very proudly cared for by Heritage New Zealand.

We're celebrating this big anniversary with a day of tours, talks, family activities, competitions, and, of course, birthday cake!

Visit our website for a developing schedule of events, and to book heritage tours and special attic tours.

This event is proudly presented by Heritage New Zealand Pouhere Taonga as part of Wellington Heritage Festival 2026.

events.name: Think Better, Live Better
events.venue:
Te Matapihi ki te Ao Nui Central Library
Wellington, Wellington
events.long_description:
Overview

Your mind is powerful but is it working for you? Join us for five practical tools that change how you think, feel and live every day.

Think Better, Live Better

A two-hour workshop that changes how you think

Most of us have never been taught how to think. We've learned what to think - at school, at work, through experience. But the actual process running in the background? The stories we tell ourselves, the patterns we fall into, the way we focus our attention, nobody really teaches that.

This workshop does.

Think Better, Live Better is a practical, engaging two-hour session grounded in real psychology and delivered in plain English. No jargon, no theory for theory's sake, and no forced positivity. Just five powerful tools you can start using the same day.

What you'll learn

Tool 1 — Change the story: Your brain defaults to the worst interpretation of any situation. Learn to catch that automatic story, question it, and replace it with a more accurate and useful one. This single shift reduces anxiety and improves decisions you make under pressure.

Tool 2 — Watch your own mind: Most of us are so inside our thoughts we never stop to look at them. This tool teaches you to step back and notice your own thinking patterns - the loops, the traps, the habits, without being swept along by them. Once you can name a pattern, you're no longer ruled by it.

Tool 3 — Get curious about what goes wrong: We've been taught to treat failure as evidence that something is wrong with us. This tool flips that. Learn to approach setbacks with curiosity rather than self-judgement, seeing the lesson, adjusting the approach, and moving forward with more confidence.

Tool 4 — Choose where your mind goes: Your brain is wired to scan for what's wrong three times more than it notices what's right. That's not a character flaw, it's biology. This tool teaches you to train your attention deliberately, so you're not at the mercy of stress, habit, and fear.

Tool 5 — Stop wrestling with your thoughts: Some thoughts don't need to be believed or fought, they just need to be noticed and let go. This tool gives you a simple, usable technique to unhook from the thoughts that hold you back, without trying to think them away.

What to expect

This is an interactive, conversational workshop, not a lecture. Expect real examples, honest discussion, a bit of laughter, and moments of reflection. Every participant receives a personal workbook to use during the session and take home, so you leave with something practical in your hands, not just in your head.

You'll finish the two hours with a complete inner toolkit and one clear commitment to yourself about how you'll use it.

This workshop is for you if:

you find yourself stuck in worry, self-doubt, or overthinking
you want to respond to pressure and setbacks more confidently
you're ready to have more control over how you think and feel
you're curious about how your mind works and ways to optimise it.

Workshop details

Duration: Two hours Includes: Personal workbook Group size: Intimate - maximum 12 participants Location: Wellington CBD

Come ready to be honest, curious, and a little bit surprised by what's possible.

events.name: This Is Grief: On the Road
events.venue: Loss & Grief Centre, 1 Kapiti Road, Paraparaumu 5032, Paraparaumu
events.long_description:
Grief is part of being human, but we still struggle to talk about it.
This Is Grief: On the Road is a free community event bringing honest conversations about grief, loss, love and the life that continues around them into communities across Aotearoa.

Join author and This Is Grief founder Kirsten O'Connor for a relaxed, human conversation about what grief really looks like, beyond the clichés, timelines and expectations we so often place around it. Kirsten will share from her own experience of grief and from her work writing and talking about loss, before opening the space for conversation and connection.

You don't need to have the right words. You don't need to share anything you don't want to. This is a space for anyone living with loss, or anyone who wants to better understand and support someone who is.

Come along, listen, talk if you'd like to, and be part of a conversation we don't have nearly often enough.

This is a free community event. Registration is recommended as places may be limited.

About this Workshop
Judy’s practical and engaging workshop is especially geared toward choral singers. Drawing on current understanding of the ageing voice, it explores the physiological changes that occur in both the brain and vocal mechanism over time, and offers practical strategies to help maintain vocal health, flexibility, and confidence. Participants will have the opportunity to apply these ideas through a series of guided group singing activities and vocal exercises.

About our clinician
Judy Bellingham is a respected singer, teacher, adjudicator, examiner, and presenter. Although retired from full-time academic and performance roles, she remains deeply committed to the transformative power of the human voice, Judy maintains a thriving private teaching studio and is a sought-after presenter of workshops and masterclasses throughout New Zealand and internationally.

A rare opportunity to explore the attic at Old Government Buildings as we celebrate its 150th birthday.

Join our expert guide for a tour around the attic at Wellington's iconic Old Government Buildings.

You'll see some fascinating (and sometimes scandalous) historic graffiti, explore the old attic filing room, and view Old Government Buildings' clock, still wound every week by hand, from the inside.

Numbers are limited to ensure everyone enjoys themselves, so booking ahead ensures your place.

Please note that this tour requires you to step over struts and at times slip through tight spaces, therefore a reasonable standard of agility and fitness is required, along with appropriate clothing for a dusty attic.

Please meet your guide at the main entrance on Lambton Quay 10 minutes prior to your tour time.

Questions? Contact us at info@heritage.org.nz or (04) 494 8320.

events.long_description:
Renowned historians Chris Pugsley and Buddy Mikaere, with local historian Neil Frances, explore New Zealand’s costly experience at Monte Cassino, including the stories of local men who took part.
The Battle of Monte Cassino was one of New Zealand’s most significant and costly campaigns of the Second World War. Military historians Chris Pugsley and Buddy Mikaere will examine the fighting, the decisions that shaped the campaign and its lasting legacy, while bringing the experience close to home through the stories of Featherston and Wairarapa servicemen who served in Italy.

events.long_description:
Architect John Scott said of Wairarapa’s woolsheds, "they are us".
Join Chris Cochran at Waiorongomai Station to explore what these remarkable buildings reveal about our region’s history.

Through rarely seen architectural drawings, photographs and stories, Chris Cochran traces the evolution of Wairarapa’s woolsheds from the earliest sheep stations to the twentieth century. Discover the architecture, ingenuity and personalities behind these iconic rural buildings, including many that still stand across the region today.

events.long_description:
Hutt Valley Rose Society Annual Rose Show!
Holy smokes, the Rose Show is less than a month away!!! That means three things!!

1. We're firing all engines to ensure the best and biggest Rose Show ever!

2. We're going to be shamelessly plugging this for the next four weeks. �

and..... (drumroll, please!)

3. It's less than a month til you have the opportunity to come to the show!

Two days of colour, fragrance, and honestly? JOY. When you walk into the room, the smell will intoxicate you, the variety and vibrancy of the roses will fascinate you.

You can see which roses won in their classes, and the wonderful Society members will be there to answer any questions you might have about why they won, and maybe where you can get some of your own!

(Join us! Join the Dark Side! Join the Society! We have cookies! No, seriously, we do actually have cookies.)

We'll have gorgeous plants from South Pacific Roses in Ōtaki for sale. We'll have beautiful posies for an insanely reasonable price to buy, for yourself or for a loved one.

And we share the annual show with the wonderful people of the Hutt Valley Horticultural Society, who always have wonderful plants and crafts for sale as well as gorgeous exhibits of their own. Literally, their dahlias have inspired some of our members to diversify.

For a tiny $3 doorcharge, come and spend a little time with us and see why we love our roses so much.

Also there's the model train show next door at the Stadium so you could do both! Tiny Trains! Stunning roses! Nice people!

Generative AI is being forced upon us by Big Tech companies chasing profit. 2000's Day Party: Wellington 🦋
The 2000’s Day Party is here!

Get Ready to Throw It Back to the 2000s! 🎉

Join us for an unforgettable day filled with the biggest hits of the 2000s, featuring chart-topping tracks from your favorite artists of the decade. Whether you’re a noughties music lover or just here for the nostalgia, this party is all about good vibes and even better tunes! 🎧💃✨

🎶 Nonstop Noughties Anthems: Sing your heart out to the iconic hits that defined the decade—from pop bangers to rnb classics and everything in between.

Let’s make it a day to remember—noughties style! 💿🎤🎉

Perfect for Stag/Hen/Birthday party’s or if you just fancy a day out with all your mates! 🪩

Expect to hear music from:

Beyoncé ⭐️ Britney Spears ⭐️ Eminem ⭐️ Justin Timberlake ⭐️ Usher ⭐️ Rihanna ⭐️ Coldplay ⭐️ Daft Punk ⭐️ Alicia Keys ⭐️ Linkin Park ⭐️ Avril Lavigne ⭐️ Green Day ⭐️ Christina Aguilera ⭐️ OutKast ⭐️ Jay-Z ⭐️ The Black Eyed Peas ⭐️ Shakira ⭐️ Kelly Clarkson ⭐️ Pink ⭐️ Ne-Yo ⭐️ Fall Out Boy ⭐️ Nickelback ⭐️ Lil Wayne ⭐️ Taylor Swift ⭐️ 50 Cent

FAQ’S

🗣️ Why do the tickets come in different price tiers?

Whilst there is no physical difference. There is only a limited amount of tickets we can sell. Therefore we operate a festival style ticketing model. The earlier you buy your ticket the cheaper it will be.

🗣️ Do you do group discount? Stag/Hen etc

Yes, we offer a discounted ticket price for groups of 10 or more. These tickets can be found listed as the “Big Group Package!” above, orders for these tickets are restricted to a minimum of 10.

🗣️ Will there be more tickets available if the event is sold out?

Once this event is sold out, there will not be any additional tickets released. In addition to this we will be unable to sell them at the door due to maximum capacity and health and safety regulations.

🗣️ Is the venue accessible?

Our events take place at a variety of locations across the UK and Ireland. As each varies please ensure to check the specific venue's website for accessibility information.

🗣️ Can I resell my tickets?

Yes, if you are unable to attend an event you are welcome to sell your tickets on. We do not use names on tickets as a condition for entry.

🗣️ Are your events 18+?

All of our events are strictly 18+. A valid photographic ID may be requested on entry.

🗣️ What do I do if I cant find my tickets or confirmation email?

We use Fatsoma to sell tickets for our events. If you’re struggling to find your ticket, you can access their support channels via https://support.fatsoma.com/support/home

🗣️ Are there tickets available on the door?

We always recommend booking in advance as we cannot guarantee on the door entry. However, in certain instances there will be a limited number of tickets on a first come first served basis for sale on the door.

🗣️ I have more questions?

If you have additional questions and wish to contact us directly, don’t hesitate to drop us a DM on either Facebook (Daytime Disco) or Instagram (@daytimediscoevents)

In-line with normal consumer standards for ticket purchases, tickets for Daytime Disco events are non-refundable, on the condition that we not moved the event or canceled it. GUARANTED TO SHIFT MORE THAT JUST AWARENESS ALONE.

events.long_description:
Create your own ring stack from copper, brass, and sterling silver in this fun and rewarding jewellery workshop.

Guided by experienced and supportive tutors, you’ll be introduced to the fundamental skills of jewellery making while creating a small collection of rings to take home.

During this 3-hour class, you’ll learn how to measure your finger, cut metal to size, and add textures and patterns using hammers and punches. You’ll also be shown how to solder your rings with a jeweller’s torch, before finishing them with filing, sanding, and polishing techniques.

By the end of the session, you’ll have crafted a thick sterling silver ring and a stack of copper or brass rings, including two plain round wires to texture as you like, and a choice of decorative brass pearl wire or square wire.

This class is ideal for beginners, groups of friends, or visitors wanting a memorable creative experience. Many students find jewellery making a mindful activity, offering a chance to slow down, work with their hands, and enjoy the rhythm of making.

The class fee includes all materials and consumables, such as solder, sandpaper, and polishing materials. Extra silver and other metals will be available for purchase in the studio for those who would like to expand their collection or upgrade one of their brass or copper wires to a second silver one.

Children aged 12 and over are welcome. Anyone under 16 must be accompanied by an enrolled parent or caregiver.

events.name: Desert Wind
events.venue: St. Michael's Anglican Church,81 Upland Road, Kelburn, Wellington, New Zealand
events.long_description:
Desert Wind
Philip Griffin | oud
Tunji Beier | percussion
Rasoul Abbasi | kamancheh
Manda Safavi | daf
Kamala Bain | recorders
Imogen Granwal | viola da gamba

Embark on an evocative journey through the rich musical traditions of the Middle East and exploring music that has been influenced by Middle Eastern traditions. This vibrant fusion features acclaimed oud player Philip Griffin and internationally renowned percussionist Tunji Beier (Australia). We are also delighted to welcome Auckland-based kamancheh player Rasoul Abassi, joining Wellington local, Kamala Bain (recorders), Imogen Granwal (viola da gamba) and Manda Safavi (daf). This exciting musical collaboration will travel through a diverse and captivating sound world, where traditions intertwine and new connections emerge. Desert Wind weaves together cultures, histories, and sounds into a mesmerising musical tapestry, revealing music as a powerful bridge between worlds.

**ART GHETTO – Latin Swing Band | Live at Park Kitchen

Experience an evening of original global grooves and Latin Swing with ART GHETTO at Park Kitchen, Miramar, Wellington.

Blending Latin rhythms, swing influences and sounds from around the world, ART GHETTO brings together an eclectic mix of musicians and instruments for a distinctive live music experience.

Led by composer and guitarist Jonathon Harper, the band features Baz Bailey on percussion and vocals, and Venezuelan-born multi-instrumentalist and vocalist Erwin La Cruz. events.venue: Stonehenge Aotearoa, Carterton, 51 Ahiaruhe Road, Ahiaruhe, Carterton
events.long_description:
Join us at Stonehenge Aotearoa, a full-scale working henge in the Wairarapa Dark Sky Reserve, for a heritage presentation exploring both European and Māori astronomical traditions. Afterwards, watch the sun set across the stones as the southern sky begins to reveal its stars. A rare chance to connect ancient heritage with modern astronomy, right here in Carterton.

Suitable for older children and adults.

Optional add-on: a specially developed ""Star Talk"" session exploring Māori astronomy and other ancient traditions (Egyptian and beyond) following by laser light guided night sky is available as a separate booking beginning 9pm.

events.id: Darren Watson Plays The Shed-46a Victoria Street, Alicetown, Lower Hutt 5010, New Zealand-Humanitix
events.name: Darren Watson Plays The Shed
events.venue: 46a Victoria Street, Alicetown, Lower Hutt 5010, New Zealand
events.long_description:
Much-loved Pōneke blues and roots singer-songwriter Darren Watson is returning to his favourite Lower Hutt intimate venue, The Shed for the third time (with special guest Matt Hay).

For this visit the ex-Chicago Smoke Shop leader, ‘Planet Key’ songwriter, and multiple NZ Music Award nominee is bringing his musical compardre Matt Hay along to both open the show and accompany Watson on harmonica.

Watson’s latest album ‘Darren Watson sings John Hiatt’ was released just over a year ago to critical acclaim, including a 4-star review in US jazz and blues ‘bible’ Downbeat, and spectacular NZ chart success.

Opener Matt Hay’s latest album ‘Dog and Pony Show’ (produced by Watson) was judged ‘Best Americana Album’ at the 2024 Aotearoa NZ Folk Alliance Awards.

“ Matt brings his beautiful songs to open the show and then joins me blowing some beautiful, tasteful harp. I’m really enjoying playing with Matt again.”

Darren says this show, while still featuring a few choice Hiatt covers, will feature more of his own material old and new.

“ I’ve got some new things on the boil, and I’m really enjoying exploring my back catalogue. There’s a surprising amount of songs after forty odd years!.”

For the uninitiated, a Darren Watson show is big on dynamics, foot stomping blues grooves, and emotional pin-drop moments. There’s politics aplenty, and an awful lot of self-deprecating humour.

Watson is well-known as a powerful guitarist but what many people only realise once they hear him live is he can really sing.

Doors open 7pm for a 7.30pm start.

events.long_description:
Acclaimed indie band Flyte bring their signature blend of heartfelt lyricism and melodic craftsmanship to a special run of New Zealand shows this November.

Flyte have earned widespread acclaim for their refined songwriting and emotionally resonant sound, with a catalogue that showcases their evolution from classic British guitar pop to more expansive and introspective arrangements. Their releases have been celebrated for their lyrical honesty and rich harmonies, cementing their place as one of the UK’s most compelling contemporary bands.

Formed in London, Flyte are led by singer-songwriters Will Taylor and Nick Hill, whose close creative partnership underpins the band’s distinctive identity. They broke through with their debut album The Loved Ones and continued to build momentum with subsequent records, including This Is Really Going to Hurt and Flyte, earning praise for their timeless influences and modern sensibility. Their work captures themes of love, vulnerability and connection, delivered with a stripped-back elegance and attention to detail that has resonated with audiences worldwide.
For audiences in Aotearoa, these shows offer a rare opportunity to experience Flyte’s intimate and immersive live performance, bringing their finely crafted songs to life with warmth, precision and emotional depth.

events.long_description:
OFFICIAL SELECTION: Venice Film Festival -
OFFICIAL SELECTION: Telluride Film Festival -
OFFICIAL SELECTION: Toronto International Film Festival -

The latest film from British cinema royalty Danny Boyle (Trainspotting, Slumdog Millionaire), Ink charts the rise of Rupert Murdoch’s notorious newspaper The Sun, and the creation of the UK’s tabloid culture.

Guy Pearce (The Brutalist) stars as Murdoch, alongside Jack O’Connell (Sinners) as newspaper editor Larry Lamb, newly assigned to oversee the fledgling daily paper. Tasked with attracting new readers in the competitive British media market, Lamb devises a new tactic - throw anything onto the page that will turn heads, no matter the veracity.

The Sun sees a massive spike in readership, and this new broad scope allows Jules Davies (Claire Foy) to break through the male-dominated hierarchy. But as the paper circulation grows, so too does the number of its critics.

Already generating awards season buzz, the fast-paced and gripping Ink features riveting performances from its star cast, in a thrilling exploration of this controversial newsroom legacy.

events.long_description:
We’re going deep.

Hailing all the way from Berlin, Vault 9 is very proud to announce:

SUBMARINE

Wellington, you’re in for another night of deep, rolling Drum & Bass! Known for a sound that sits in the deep end of the genre, Submarine will bring you liquid melodies, halftime arrangements and minimal madness for a journey unlike anything that has blessed your ears. With an insane catalogue on labels such as 1985 Music, Demand Records and Flexout Audio, he’s well equipped to deliver a set that won’t be forgotten.

We’ve also hand-picked a support crew that, alongside Submarine, will take the night to another level: DXN, Louder, Intec, Pearly, Gunn, Zillah, Fe, Java all being hosted by Timmy P… Wellington’s finest. These selectas have been sculpted by the gods to bring you only the very best selections known to man, and they’ll ensure your legs are skanking with your bass faces on. All. Damn. Night.

As our very first international artist, we couldn’t be happier to show Submarine what Wellington’s made of. We’ve wanted to bring a headliner from overseas for a long time and are finally getting it done, with a producer whose sound fits our city’s vibe to a T!

The lineup is stacked, the date is set, and the venue is pumped. We’ll be delivering vibes that are deep, melodic and memorable. Even Eminem would tell you this opportunity comes once in a lifetime, so don’t miss it. Get your tickets ASAP!

Afters @ 38 Dixon Street 

Friday 14 November 9pm - 3am

Tix via Humanitix (link in bio)

18+

events.name: Greentea Peng tickets
events.venue: Meow Nui, Wellington, New Zealand
events.long_description:
Presented by: Astral People & Handsome Tours
Neo-soul artist Greentea Peng arrives in Australia and New Zealand this November, delicately infusing hypnotic dub with seductive hip-hop swings and jazzy neo-soul excursions.
The South London born Greentea Peng is an artist whose work is guided by self-inquiry, shaped by the dualities she inhabits: pain and pleasure, engagement and withdrawal, expression and stillness. Her emotional literacy is transformed into a blend of neo-soul, dub and jazz, all draped in psychedelic textures.
After rediscovering her love for music while travelling - where she joined a local band in Mexico - a renewed sense of self-confidence propelled her return to London and the release of her 2018 EP, Sensi. The project marked the beginning of a distinctive sound carved from heavy, weighty narration, dubby grain, hissy textures and sparse arrangements. The six-track release is anchored by negative space that sits tightly side-chained to the kick, creating a breathing, pumping feel, while minimal melodic movements allow tension to build and swell around her earthy, soulful voice.
This early foundation continued to evolve, punctuated by notable moments such as her performance of "Downers" on COLORS, which garnered millions of views, as well as her television debut on Later... with Jools Holland on the BBC, where she performed her breakout track "Hu Man". These milestones paved the way for her 2021 debut album, MAN MADE, which she described as a record designed to resonate "more in your heart space, and less in your headspace".
Her latest offering, TELL DEM IT'S SUNNY, dives deeper into her enduring practice of self-witnessing - a work of affirmation, emotional maturity and radical self-acceptance. From "BALI SKIT PT. 1", a soundscape that rises and falls like the ribcage of a shadowy spirit, to "RAW", where we're once again met with Peng's poignant voice notes, the album showcases an artist continuing to explore her inner world with clarity and conviction.
Now, the psychedelic R&B soulstress returns to Australia and New Zealand this November, bringing her rich catalogue of deeply personal, genre-defying music to audiences once again.

events.id: Carkeek Revealed: A Walk Through Wairarapa’s Astronomical Heritage-Pae Tū Mōkai O Tauira Whare, 23 N Soldiers Settlement Road, Featherston-Event Finder
events.name: Carkeek Revealed: A Walk Through Wairarapa’s Astronomical Heritage
events.venue: Pae Tū Mōkai O Tauira Whare, 23 N Soldiers Settlement Road, Featherston
events.long_description:
Step into the past as we uncover the story of Stephen Carkeek and his passion for the night sky. The Carkeek observatory - the oldest surviving example of an astronomical observatory in New Zealand - was rediscovered in 1987.

Take a family-friendly guided walk to see the remains, now covered and protected, and hear stories from Stephen's descendants as well as passionate local advocates keen to protect this piece of history. Enjoy a morning tea and listen to a reading of the children's book The Lost Star of Featherston.

Built in circa 1867 on a farm south of the Wairarapa town of Featherston, the Carkeek Observatory possesses outstanding historical significance as Aotearoa/New Zealand’s earliest surviving astronomical observatory. Built by civil servant, timeball instigator and amateur astronomer Stephen Carkeek, the place reflects the crucial role of amateur practitioners in the foundation and development of science in this country.

Koha.

events.name: Glass Mosaic Day
events.venue: Workspace Studios Ōtaki, 2 Arthur Street, Ōtaki, Ōtaki
events.long_description:
This day class will cover making small, interior mosaics on wood bases using stunning brightly coloured glass.

Small mosaics are really quick and simple to make - and can create a real design punch with colourful glass pieces and a range of really nice backing shapes and frames. This is a great place to start if you want to get into Mosaics, and work up to glass-on-glass, exterior mosaics or three-D mosaics.

You can choose from either :
A micro set of mosaics - suitable for tiny wall-sets or bespoke heirloom ornaments
Box framed bases, ready to hang.
A range of simple cut-out shapes that could be hung on a wall or mounted on doors.

The class covers:
Preparing your bases and materials, choosing adhesives that suit interior projects.
Planning and choosing simple designs to make your mosaics really pop
How to snip your glass down into tiny pieces if needed (most pieces are already cut for you)
Working with adhesives, tips and tricks with tools.

Finally we will cover grouting and finishing your mosaics - due to the time it takes for grout to fully cure, some cleanup and final sealing coats will need to be done later on at home, you’ll be given clear instructions and the sealant to apply at the end of the class.

We can also look at options for hanging and mounting - we have some simple fittings for you to choose from.

Some students may finish in time to grout your pieces - seeing these pieces are SO small, they are often dry enough for grouting. Or you can take your grout away to do at home, or leave with us to grout for you and collect in a few days. (There’s a small fee attached to that part.)

This is a warm, friendly class with excellent support and learning for complete beginners and those who want to start working with hand-cut glass terraria.

All tools are supplied, though you are welcome to bring your own tools and glass if you have them.
Materials for the main class projects are supplied as part of your course fee.

Young makers aged 12 and up are welcome to join the class, as long as they are able to work safely with sharp glass and tools.

Anyone under the age of 16 must attend with an enrolled parent or caregiver who is there to support them and participate alongside them.

events.long_description:
Our on-farm Craft Open Days are aimed primarily at knitters, spinners, crocheters and other fibre crafters.

Nestled in the small rural community of Tinui is Rewa Rewa Station. Operating as a hill country Sheep & Beef breeding farm with a strong focus on NZ Wool & Fibre. Romney, Corriedale cross Romney, Polwarth & Gotland sheep provide the fleeces to create fibre products for crafters, which are sold via the Rewa Rewa Station website, and at Fibre Markets. Our Studio Shop is also open during Craft Days or by appointment outside of these days.

Our Craft Days allow you to work on your own project, seek advice, learn a new fibre skill or maybe just spend time with fellow fibre crafters while potentially ticking off a project or two in the process.

Please bring your knitting, crocheting, spinning, hand sewing, or any project you are working on and enjoy a drive in the country!

Coffee, tea and snacks provided, but bring your lunch and stay awhile.

Everyone is welcome, the more the merrier!

Note: Craft Days are primarily held on the 3rd Saturday of every mont,h but occasionally we do have to juggle the dates.

events.venue: Hidden Lakes, Masterton
events.long_description:
North of Masterton are 2 hidden lakes, formed when the 1855 earthquake re-routed the Ruamahanga River.

The old route was cut off by the earthquake and formed 2 small lakes.

The lakes are on private land, and the Wairarapa Walking Festival has secured permission to take a small group to walk to the Lakes.

Join local writer, researcher and storyteller Joe Potangaroa (Ngati Kahungunu, Rangitane, Tuhoe, English) who will participate, and share his knowledge of tikanga, taiao and Wairarapa history.

We also hope to have a local botanist join in to explain the flora and fauna of the area and recent restoration plantings.

A small bus will be provided to transport registered walkers to the location.

Note the track is uneven with moderate hills to walk up.

Please follow any Health and Safety advice from the landowners as the walk crosses private land.

events.name: Stacking Rings - November Taster
events.venue: Workspace Studios Wellington Market Lane, 3 Market Lane, Wellington Cenral, Wellington
events.long_description:
Create your own ring stack from copper, brass, and sterling silver in this fun and rewarding jewellery workshop!

Guided by experienced and supportive tutors, you’ll be introduced to the fundamental skills of jewellery making while creating a small collection of rings to take home.

During this 3-hour class, you’ll learn how to measure your finger, cut metal to size, and add textures and patterns using hammers and punches. You’ll also be shown how to solder your rings with a jeweller’s torch, before finishing them with filing, sanding, and polishing techniques.

By the end of the session, you’ll have crafted a thick sterling silver ring and a stack of copper or brass rings, including two plain round wires to texture as you like, and a choice of decorative brass pearl wire or square wire.

This class is ideal for beginners, groups of friends, or visitors wanting a memorable creative experience. Many students find jewellery making a mindful activity, offering a chance to slow down, work with their hands, and enjoy the rhythm of making.

The class fee includes all materials and consumables, such as solder, sandpaper, and polishing materials. Extra silver and other metals will be available for purchase in the studio for those who would like to expand their collection or upgrade one of their brass or copper wires to a second silver one.

Children aged 12 and over are welcome. Anyone under 16 must be accompanied by an enrolled parent or caregiver.

events.id: Tones of Silence; Futuna Chapel in B&W (Public Talk-John Walsh, Patrick Reynolds, Andrew Barrie)-Futuna Close, off Friend Street, Karori, New Zealand 6012,55 Friend St, Karori, Wellington 6012, New Zealand, Wellington-All Events In
events.name: Tones of Silence; Futuna Chapel in B&W (Public Talk-John Walsh, Patrick Reynolds, Andrew Barrie)
events.venue: Futuna Close, off Friend Street, Karori, New Zealand 6012,55 Friend St, Karori, Wellington 6012, New Zealand, Wellington
events.long_description:
Tones of Silence; Futuna Chapel in B&W (Public Talk-John Walsh, Patrick Reynolds, Andrew Barrie)
Architecture writer John Walsh and photographer Patrick Reynolds discuss their city walking guides and the heritage places they reveal, bringing together Walsh’s deep knowledge of Aotearoa New Zealand architecture and Reynolds’ distinctive photographic eye.

About the speakers
John Walsh is a leading New Zealand architecture writer. He edited Architecture New Zealand magazine for a decade, and has written numerous books on New Zealand architecture, among them the newly revised Auckland Architecture: A Walking Guide, which features photographs by Patrick Reynolds.

Patrick Reynolds is probably best known for his exceptional architectural and interior photographs that appear in publications such as Urbis and Vogue Living. However, over the past 20 years he has developed a highly successful parallel career as a leading photographer within New Zealand contemporary visual arts. As an exhibiting artist his work is about New Zealand landscape, nature, architecture, patterns of seeing, and – just as importantly – about the art and place of photography.

Professor Andrew Barrie
New Zealand-born architectural critic and designer, Prof. Andrew Barrie discusses the research and publication of Block maps, drawing on his work as an architectural critic, designer, author, and educator with deep connections to architecture in Japan and Aotearoa New Zealand.

About the speaker
Professor Andrew Barrie is a New Zealand-born architectural critic and designer formerly based in Tokyo. After completing doctoral studies in Japan, Andrew was a project architect in the office of Toyo Ito, one of the world’s most innovative and influential architects, and later at Cheshire Architects in Auckland. Andrew own design work is widely celebrated, having won numerous awards in both Japan and NZ, including a prestigious named award from the New Zealand Institute of Architects—and has been exhibited nationally and internationally. He is a regular contributor to architecture and design journals and has authored three books on the work of Japanese architects. He has made significant contributions to architectural culture in New Zealand, recognized by the award (with the Block Foundation) of the NZIA’s Auckland Cup for services to architecture, and his election to the Royal Society of New Zealand.

Please bring a yoga mat, pillow, eye mask and blanket - or whatever it is you need to feel most warm and comfortable

Discover the transformative effects of sound therapy with this 1-hour gong bath experience.

During this session, participants will be surrounded by the resonant vibrations of gongs, carefully designed to induce deep states of relaxation and calm. As you settle into the experience, allow the soothing tones to wash over you, releasing tension and promoting a sense of inner peace.

Scientific studies have highlighted the benefits of sound therapy, particularly gong baths, in reducing stress and promoting overall well-being. The rhythmic patterns and overtones of the gongs can help entrain brainwaves, leading to a meditative state and improved mental clarity.

Beyond the immediate effects, many participants report experiencing lasting benefits such as improved sleep, reduced anxiety, and enhanced mood following a gong bath session. By immersing yourself in the healing vibrations of the gongs, you can tap into a deeper sense of relaxation and rejuvenation.

Whether you're looking to unwind after a long day or explore new avenues of self-care, this 1-hour gong bath offers a unique opportunity to reconnect with yourself and find balance amidst the hustle and bustle of daily life. There will be cups of tea available afterwards to help us integrate and ground.

THIS EVENT IS RESTRICTED TO 40 PEOPLE ONLY

Disclaimer
Gong baths are safe and supportive for most people. However, please consult your doctor or mental health professional before attending if you:-have a pacemaker or other implanted medical device
-live with epilepsy or a sound-sensitive condition
-are in the first trimester of pregnancy
-are experiencing severe or unmanaged mental health challenges (such as psychosis, schizophrenia, or PTSD)If you have recent injuries, surgeries, or other health concerns, let me know so we can make sure you’re comfortable.

Everyone responds differently to sound. If at any point during the session you feel overwhelmed or uncomfortable, you are welcome to sit up, move gently, or step outside. Your wellbeing always comes first.

About Me

TICKETS ON SALE NOW: https://go.astralpeople.com/gtp-wlg

Neo-soul artist Greentea Peng arrives in Australia and New Zealand this November, delicately infusing hypnotic dub with seductive hip-hop swings and jazzy neo-soul excursions.

The South London born Greentea Peng is an artist whose work is guided by self-inquiry, shaped by the dualities she inhabits: pain and pleasure, engagement and withdrawal, expression and stillness. Her emotional literacy is transformed into a blend of neo-soul, dub and jazz, all draped in psychedelic textures.

After rediscovering her love for music while travelling - where she joined a local band in Mexico - a renewed sense of self-confidence propelled her return to London and the release of her 2018 EP, Sensi. The project marked the beginning of a distinctive sound carved from heavy, weighty narration, dubby grain, hissy textures and sparse arrangements. The six-track release is anchored by negative space that sits tightly side-chained to the kick, creating a breathing, pumping feel, while minimal melodic movements allow tension to build and swell around her earthy, soulful voice.

This early foundation continued to evolve, punctuated by notable moments such as her performance of "Downers" on COLORS, which garnered millions of views, as well as her television debut on Later... with Jools Holland on the BBC, where she performed her breakout track "Hu Man". These milestones paved the way for her 2021 debut album, MAN MADE, which she described as a record designed to resonate "more in your heart space, and less in your headspace".

Her latest offering, TELL DEM IT'S SUNNY, dives deeper into her enduring practice of self-witnessing - a work of affirmation, emotional maturity and radical self-acceptance. From "BALI SKIT PT. 1", a soundscape that rises and falls like the ribcage of a shadowy spirit, to "RAW", where we're once again met with Peng's poignant voice notes, the album showcases an artist continuing to explore her inner world with clarity and conviction.

Now, the psychedelic R&B soulstress returns to Australia and New Zealand this November, bringing her rich catalogue of deeply personal, genre-defying music to audiences once again.

events.long_description:
Join English classicist and historian Dame Mary Beard in Wellington for a night packed with witty stories and surprising facts. An Evening with Mary Beard: Talking Classics plays at The Opera House in Wellington. The show is built around her new book, ‘Talking Classics: The Shock of the Old’. A guest host joins Mary and will round out the evening with a Q&A. If you have burning questions about Roman emperors or 4,000-year-old bread, now is the time to have them answered.   

Mary has made a career around refusing to let the ancient world stay ancient. She’s authored more than 20 books, including ‘SPQR’ and ‘Emperor of Rome’. These books helped popularise Roman history while staying true to her academic roots (she had a 40-year career at the University of Cambridge). She’s appeared on television programmes from Roman history documentaries to ‘The Grand Tour’.   

Expect an unpretentious and informative evening. On your way out, pick up a copy of ‘Talking Classics’. Get the book signed by Mary, and leave feeling more knowledgeable than when you walked in.

events.venue: Toi Aro,3 Market Lane, Wellington, New Zealand
events.long_description:
He Kōrerorero: A Conversation about Indigenous Dramaturgy (Writers Workshop)
He Kōrerorero is an ongoing conversation about the practice of Indigenous dramaturgy in Aotearoa and Te Whenua Moemoeā, Australia.

In conversation with award-winning writer, director and producer Hone Kouka (Ngāti Porou, Ngāti Raukawa, Ngāti Kahungunu) and Birribay, Worrimay theatremaker and academic Dr.Liza-Mare Syron. He Kōrerorero will share insights into their dramaturgical practice of the development of new Indigenous writing. He Kōrerorero will workshop and discuss the evolution of Indigenous dramaturgy and share tools for managing this practice within the Indigenous arts sector today. Hone and Dr. Liza-Mare will include both playwriting and screenwriting as part of their discussions.

This workshop is relevant for scriptwriters, theatremakers, filmmakers, producers and developers who are working across both stage and screen.

A theatre maker and academic, Liza-Mare is an Associate Professor Scientia in the School of Arts and Media at UNSW and the Co-Associate Dean Indigenous in the Faculty of Arts, Design and Architecture. As a founding member of Moogahlin Performing Arts, NSW’s leading Aboriginal Theatre company, Liza-Mare has directed, produced, and been a dramaturge of many award-winning productions such as The Visitors by Marrawarri playwright Jane Harrison and The Weekend by Kuku Yalanji playwright Henrietta Baird.

Hone Kouka (Ngāti Porou, Ngāti Raukawa, Ngāti Kahungunu) is a father, a member of the New Zealand Order of Merit, an acclaimed Māori writer, producer and director, the youngest winner of the Bruce Mason Playwriting Award. In 2022, Hone was named an Arts Foundation Te Tumu Toi Laureate, receiving the Sir Roger Hall Theatre Award. Hone’s plays include Ngā Tangata Toa, Waiora: Te Ūkaipō, The Prophet and Bless The Child. In 2004, Hone co-founded the production company, Tawata Productions, focusing on the development and presentation of new theatre by Māori and Pasifika artists. Hone is the co-founder of Kia Mau Festival.

Breaking Ground returns for another year of intensive Indigenous new writing. Our festival has created space for bold and brilliant new works in Te Whanganui-a-Tara since its inception in 2010. Artists are a vital part of our communities and the current landscape presents fewer and fewer opportunities for us to gather, to wānanga, and to create. The 2026 programme responds to the growing need to hold on to spaces where writers can thrive and where the iconic stories of tomorrow can be unearthed.

https://tawataproductions.com/breaking-ground/

He Kōrerorero is presented from 10AM-1PM Tuesday November 17 2026 at the Toi Aro, 3 Market Lane, Te Aro, Wellington.

There are only 12 spaces offered for this workshop.

Breaking Ground is produced by Te Whanganui-a-Tara based creative company, Tawata Productions, and made possible by our partners Toi Aro, Wellington City Council and Creative New Zealand.

events.long_description:
Hailing from the music-filled streets of Melbourne, Australia, Shaun Kirk is an award-winning blues and soul troubadour recognised for his exceptional talent as a born entertainer. His unique talent has not only earned him many accolades but also much praise from fellow artists, such as three-time Grammy Award Winner Fantastic Negrito, who has declared his show as "One of the best one-man shows he’s ever seen!"

Kirk's vocals exude a gritty, soulful depth that seems to transcend far beyond his years, with critics continually acclaiming him as "one of the finest blues voices Australia has ever heard" (Buzz Mag). Complementing his vocal artistry, Kirk's vintage guitar tones and raw grooves pay tribute to the timeless influences that have shaped his musical journey, resulting in a distinctive sound fast becoming his own.

Shaun’s musical journey has taken him to stages all over the world, where he's not only performed but consistently sold out shows, leaving audiences enthralled by his magnetic presence. From iconic festival stages like Bluesfest Byron Bay, where he's become a familiar name, to sharing the billing with legends like Robert Plant of Led Zeppelin, John Mayer, Paolo Nutini, John Butler Trio, and The Teskey Brothers; Kirk's artistic prowess is in esteemed company. Moreover, he's also had the honour of opening for household names such as blues maestro Joe Bonamassa, soul sensation Allen Stone, and the indomitable Beth Hart; further solidifying his place in the landscape of contemporary music. This remarkable journey is a testament to Kirk's unmatched talent and ability to connect with audiences across genres and generations.

WHAT THE PRESS IS SAYING ABOUT SHAUN KIRK

“It’s rare to see someone bring down the house as an opener, but Australia’s Shaun Kirk did exactly that. He connected with the crowd immediately” – Soundcheck Entertainment, Canada

“One of the most explosive acts Australia has to offer” – Mixdown Magazine, Australia

"My faith in this generation’s music has been restored.” - Dearhead Press

“Simply astounding." - Forte Magazine, Australia

events.long_description:
Overview

Helping managers and people leaders in New Zealand regulatory agencies navigate AI-enabled change with confidence.

Programme Details
Dates: Wednesday, 18 November & Thursday, 19 November
Time: 9:00 am – 1:00 pm daily (2-day interactive workshop)
Location: MartinJenkins, Wellington
Investment: $1,400 + GST per seat
Capacity: Strictly limited to 10 participants to ensure an interactive, small-group experience.
Facilitators: Cat Moody & Jarred Griffiths
The Leadership Challenge

Artificial intelligence is creating new opportunities across the public sector, but technology is only part of the story. For many leaders, the immediate challenge is helping people adapt. Teams are asking questions about changing work practices, emerging capabilities, workforce impacts, and what these changes mean for their day-to-day roles.

Leaders are increasingly expected to communicate clearly, manage uncertainty, respond to concerns, maintain engagement, and support learning while organisational approaches continue to evolve.

Leading People Through AI-Enabled Change has been designed to help people leaders meet these challenges. Rather than teaching AI tools, the programme focuses on the practical leadership skills needed to guide teams through change.

Who This Programme Is For

This programme is designed specifically for people leaders within New Zealand regulatory agencies and public sector bodies, including:

Managers
Team leaders
Anyone responsible for supporting people through organisational change

No technical background or AI expertise is required.

What Participants Will Gain

By the end of the programme, participants will be better equipped to:

Understand the unique people impacts of AI-enabled change
Recognise and address common concerns and resistance
Lead teams through uncertainty and ambiguity
Build confidence and trust during periods of change
Communicate effectively about emerging technologies and organisational shifts
Support adaptation, continuous learning, and experimentation
Apply practical leadership approaches immediately within their own teams




Programme Structure
Day 1: Understanding the change and leading through uncertainty

Wednesday, 18 November | 9:00 am – 1:00 pm

Leaders explore the people impacts of AI-enabled change and their role in guiding teams through it. They will understand how to assess readiness, communicate honestly, and build psychological safety in regulatory and public sector settings.

What will be covered
The leadership context for AI-driven change
How people respond to change and uncertainty
Change readiness and leadership responsibilities
Building trust through clear, credible communication
Crafting messages leaders can use with their teams
Reflecting on risks and opportunities in own context
Day 2: Engaging teams and turning change into action

Thursday, 19 November | 9:00 am – 1:00 pm

The focus shifts from understanding change to leading it. This will include sustaining engagement and motivation, applying frameworks to real situations, and leaving with a practical plan for adoption.

What will be covered
Team engagement and motivation during change
Applying practical change leadership frameworks
Responding to resistance, fear and scepticism
Supporting learning and capability development
Safe experimentation and responsible adoption
Pulse checks, action planning and next steps




Learning Approach

This is a highly interactive, small-group programme built around:

Facilitated discussion

It’s a 70s rock musical of biblical proportions, and it’s back. Jesus Christ Superstar is heading to St James Theatre, and Wellington audiences are in for a treat. Leading People Through AI-Enabled Change (November)
Helping managers and people leaders in New Zealand regulatory agencies navigate AI-enabled change with confidence.

About this Event


Programme Details
Dates: Wednesday, 18 November & Thursday, 19 November
Time: 9:00 am – 1:00 pm daily (2-day interactive workshop)
Location: MartinJenkins, Wellington
Investment: $1,400 + GST per seat
Capacity: Strictly limited to 10 participants to ensure an interactive, small-group experience.
Facilitators: Cat Moody & Jarred Griffiths

The Leadership Challenge

Artificial intelligence is creating new opportunities across the public sector, but technology is only part of the story. For many leaders, the immediate challenge is helping people adapt. Teams are asking questions about changing work practices, emerging capabilities, workforce impacts, and what these changes mean for their day-to-day roles.

Leaders are increasingly expected to communicate clearly, manage uncertainty, respond to concerns, maintain engagement, and support learning while organisational approaches continue to evolve.

Leading People Through AI-Enabled Change has been designed to help people leaders meet these challenges. Rather than teaching AI tools, the programme focuses on the practical leadership skills needed to guide teams through change.


Who This Programme Is For

This programme is designed specifically for people leaders within New Zealand regulatory agencies and public sector bodies, including:

Managers
Team leaders
Anyone responsible for supporting people through organisational change

No technical background or AI expertise is required.


What Participants Will Gain

By the end of the programme, participants will be better equipped to:

Understand the unique people impacts of AI-enabled change
Recognise and address common concerns and resistance
Lead teams through uncertainty and ambiguity
Build confidence and trust during periods of change
Communicate effectively about emerging technologies and organisational shifts
Support adaptation, continuous learning, and experimentation
Apply practical leadership approaches immediately within their own teams





Programme Structure
Day 1: Understanding the change and leading through uncertainty

Wednesday, 18 November | 9:00 am – 1:00 pm

Leaders explore the people impacts of AI-enabled change and their role in guiding teams through it. They will understand how to assess readiness, communicate honestly, and build psychological safety in regulatory and public sector settings.


What will be covered
The leadership context for AI-driven change
How people respond to change and uncertainty
Change readiness and leadership responsibilities
Building trust through clear, credible communication
Crafting messages leaders can use with their teams
Reflecting on risks and opportunities in own context

Day 2: Engaging teams and turning change into action

Thursday, 19 November | 9:00 am – 1:00 pm

The focus shifts from understanding change to leading it. This will include sustaining engagement and motivation, applying frameworks to real situations, and leaving with a practical plan for adoption.


What will be covered
Team engagement and motivation during change
Applying practical change leadership frameworks
Responding to resistance, fear and scepticism
Supporting learning and capability development
Safe experimentation and responsible adoption
Pulse checks, action planning and next steps





Learning Approach

This is a highly interactive, small-group programme built around:

Facilitated discussion
Real public sector examples
Practical leadership tools and frameworks
Small-group exercises and peer learning
Application to participants' own workplace contexts

Participants are encouraged to bring current challenges and opportunities from their own organisations.


Why This Programme Is Different

Many AI learning programmes focus purely on technology and software tools. Leading People Through AI-Enabled Change focuses on the leadership challenge.

Successful adoption of new technologies depends on people. This programme equips leaders with practical approaches for helping teams adapt, engage, learn, and perform during periods of transformation.


About the Facilitators

Cat Moody & Jarred Griffiths

This programme combines deep expertise in change leadership and AI transformation. Cat Moody and Jarred Griffiths bring practical experience supporting public sector organisations through organisational change, workforce transitions, leadership development, and AI adoption.

Participants will benefit from real examples, lessons learned, and practical insights drawn from current, hands-on work across public sector agencies.

Wellington City Chorus is a chapter of SingUnited International (formally Sweet Adelines) and was formed in 1998. This local chorus of dedicated and talented singers is a non-profit organisation dedicated to teaching, learning and singing four-part barbershop style harmony through performances and education opportunities.

Wellington City Chorus is led by co-directors David Brooks and Jo Hodgson. David is a master-director with over 30 years of experience as a singer, director, adjudicator, coach and arranger of barbershop music; Jo, a singing teacher and performer from the musical theatre and choral worlds, is a recent convert to this fun and challenging style.

As previous National champions, Wellington City Chorus has represented Aotearoa New Zealand on the international stage several times and looks forward to sharing a taste of Aotearoa in Australia next year.

We meet on Monday evenings, 7:00pm – 9:30pm at Wellington Bridge Club, 17 Tinakori Rd. We welcome women and non-binary singers who enjoy singing and are keen to learn, grow and perform in a supportive and welcoming environment.

About the film

Khartoum is about the 'Five lives, one city, a nation at war. A civil servant, a tea lady, a resistance committee volunteer and two street boys. Five stories from Sudan weave together in search of freedom through animated dreams, street revolutions and a war from the metropolis of Khartoum to escape in East Africa.'

The film will be introduced by SANA whānau, with a brief introduction to the exhibition, the ongoing war in Sudan, and ways to be part of the solidarity movement. Koha from this screening will go to a collective or organisation selected by SANA.

6:20pm — Film begins

About SANA

Sudan Advocacy Network Aotearoa (SANA) is a Sudanese-led organisation advancing human rights, civilian protection and solidarity with Sudan. Its creative, youth and community engagement platform, Do You Still Dream? (DYSD), amplifies Sudanese voices through arts, storytelling and public dialogue. Date my Queer Mate
We are back because you loved it so much last time!

Looking for a date? Who better to sing your praises than your mate?

Join us for the global phenomenon Date My Mate! But this time it’s QUEER! Come and flirt, mix, pash and dance!
﻿
The Good Sex Project Podcast and Emily Writes welcome you to Date My (Queer) Mate. This is a queer, trans inclusionary FLINTAQ* event. Equal parts comedy show, PowerPoint night, and match-making good time - come and mingle with dates and mates!
﻿
5pm doors open
6pm presentations start
﻿
How it works
Upon arrival, you grab a badge to say if you're looking for dates OR mates.
﻿
Friends take the stage with a 3-5 minute slide deck to pitch their mates. If you're interested in pitching a mate, please register here:

YOU MUST REGISTER TO BE IN WITH A CHANCE TO PRESENT
﻿
No stress if you aren't keen to pitch or be pitched; we need many audience babes - that's you!
﻿
Once pitches are done, there will be time to mingle and meet.
﻿
FLINTAQ* = FLINTA is a German acronym that stands for "Frauen, Lesben, Intergeschlechtliche, nichtbinäre, trans und agender Personen", meaning women, lesbians, intersex, non-binary, trans and agender people. The asterisk represents all non-binary gender identities. To explicitly include queer individuals, the term FLINTAQ is sometimes used. This includes bisexual and pansexual folks!

This event is ENM friendly.
﻿

Tumunu Writers Gathering | Breaking Ground Festival
Join us at Hannah Playhouse at this whakawhanaungatanga event for our creative hapori. This will be a chance to catch up, get to know other writers, and enjoy a relaxed quiz night.

Tumunu is a free event and is part of our wider schedule of public events for Breaking Ground.

Breaking Ground returns for another year of intensive Indigenous new writing. Our festival has created space for bold and brilliant new works in Te Whanganui-a-Tara since its inception in 2010. Artists are a vital part of our communities and the current landscape presents fewer and fewer opportunities for us to gather, to wānanga, and to create. The 2026 programme responds to the growing need to hold on to spaces where writers can thrive and where the iconic stories of tomorrow can be unearthed.

Check out our other events here:
https://tawataproductions.com/breaking-ground/

Breaking Ground is produced by Te Whanganui-a-Tara based creative company, Tawata Productions, and made possible by our partners Toi Aro, Wellington City Council and Creative New Zealand.

events.name: Jesus Christ Superstar
events.venue: St James Theatre, 77-87 Courtenay Place, Wellington
events.long_description:
Following acclaimed and sold-out runs in London as well as an extensive tour of North America, the UK, and Australia, the Olivier Award-winning reimagined production of Tim Rice and Andrew Lloyd Webber celebrated musical JESUS CHRIST SUPERSTAR will play in Auckland, Wellington and Christchurch this October through to December, as part of a major international tour.

Featuring lyrics and music by Emmy, GRAMMY, Oscar, and Tony winners Tim Rice and Andrew Lloyd Webber, this production was reimagined by London’s Regent’s Park Open Air Theatre, where it originated, and is helmed by director Timothy Sheader and choreographer Drew McOnie. Completing the creative team is design by Tom Scutt, lighting design by Lee Curran, sound design by Nick Lidster, and music supervision by Tom Deering.

A global phenomenon that has wowed audiences for decades, JESUS CHRIST SUPERSTAR is a timeless work that explores the biblical portrayal of the extraordinary events that led to the death and resurrection of Jesus Christ as seen through the eyes of his betrayer, Judas Iscariot. The story, told entirely through song, explores the personal relationships and struggles among Jesus, Judas, Mary Magdalene, Jesus’ disciples, his followers and the Roman Empire. Originally released as a concept album, the iconic 1970s rock score contains such well-known numbers as ‘Superstar’, ‘I Don’t Know How to Love Him’, and ‘Gethsemane’.

The Little Grimley Amateur Dramatic Society from Limelight Theatre returns in another hilarious comedy from David Tristram. With a membership of just four, the society has survived budget constraints, artistic disagreements, and countless theatrical disasters. This time, faced with the challenge of finding a suitable play, chairman Gordon decides there’s only one solution: an evening of Shakespeare.

After all, what could possibly go wrong when an amateur dramatic group takes on the world’s greatest playwright?

As Gordon’s ambitious vision collides with limited resources, Bernard’s enthusiastic improvisation, Joyce’s personal distractions, and Margaret’s diva tendencies, the production quickly descends into chaos. With tempers flaring, egos colliding, and Shakespeare being interpreted in ways he never intended, keeping the show on track becomes a performance in itself.

Packed with the witty dialogue, larger-than-life characters, and laugh-out-loud moments that have made the Little Grimley series a favourite with audiences, To Be Or Not To Bother is a delightful evening of pure comedy entertainment.
