events.id: WOBIL: Wise Old Bugger in Lycra-The Opera House, Wellington, New Zealand-Wellington NZ
events.name: WOBIL: Wise Old Bugger in Lycra
events.venue: The Opera House, Wellington, New Zealand
events.long_description:
The last in a trilogy of cycling-themed plays skids into The Wellington Opera House in May.  Writer-director Gregory Cooper and seasoned Kiwi actor Mark Hadlow collaborate once more to bring their cycling trilogy to a close. The one-man play 'WOBIL: Wise Old Bugger in Lycra' follows previous installments ‘MAMIL: Middle Aged Man In Lycra’ and ‘GOMIL: Grumpy Old Man In Lycra’. Expect familiar faces, trademark physical comedy, plenty of laughs, and a fair bit of heart too.
Mark is one of New Zealand’s best-known actors. You might have seen him on screen in ‘King Kong’ or ‘The Hobbit’, or a host of live professional theatre shows on stages around the motu.  Gregory's past work includes ‘That Bloody Woman’. This latest chapter sends Wayne on his hardest hill climb yet. With help, and hindrance, from a few old friends and enemies, he’s determined to go out in a blaze of lycra glory. Get ready for one last spin through friendship, ageing, and resilience.

events.long_description:
Presented by: Destroy All Lines
British legends Squeeze are returning to New Zealand in April 2027 with their Tried, Tested and Trixies Tour, celebrating 53 years of classic songwriting and standout music hits from one of the UK’s pioneers of Brit-pop music.
Founded in 1974 by Chris Difford and Glenn Tilbrook, Squeeze are one of pop’s best-loved bands with a catalogue of sky-high classics such as ‘Up the Junction’, ‘Tempted’, ‘Cool for Cats’, ‘Another Nail in My Heart’ and ‘Labelled with Love’, whose live shows are legendary and, as The Guardian wrote, “pop perfection”.
Squeeze remain one of the most revered and distinctive music outfits in UK pop history. Led by the unparalleled songwriting duo Glenn Tilbrook and Chris Difford, their legacy spans over five decades of masterful songwriting, stellar live performance, and cultural impact; between 1978 and 1996 they had no fewer than 11 singles in the UK Top 40, with six in the Top 20. Many more of their songs have been woven into the very fabric of the British songwriting tradition – alongside those of The Beatles and The Kinks – influencing everyone from Lily Allen to The Killers.
Coming to New Zealand to mark 50+ years of Squeeze and celebrate the release of their new album, Trixies, will be Glenn Tilbrook, bassist Owen Biddle, percussionist Steve Smith, keyboardist Stephen Large, drummer Simon Hanson, guitarist Leon Tilbrook and backing vocalist Danica Dora.

Portland, Oregon producer, singer-songwriter and storyteller John Craigie returns to New Zealand in April 2027 on his I Swam Here Tour.
 
Following his first New Zealand shows in 2025, Craigie returns with his latest album, I Swam Here, out now on Zabriskie Point Records. Written and produced by Craigie, the album was recorded between New Orleans and Astoria, Oregon, bringing together the musical spirit of the Gulf Coast with the quieter sounds of the Pacific Northwest.
 
For more than a decade, Craigie has built a devoted following through his warm, sharply observed songwriting and live shows that pair music with humour and storytelling. His touring has taken him across the U.S., Europe and Australia, with appearances at Newport Folk, Pickathon, Edmonton Folk Festival and High Sierra, and performances alongside artists including Gregory Alan Isakov, Sierra Hull, Brett Dennen and Jack Johnson.
 

I Swam Here follows 2024’s Pagan Church, Craigie’s collaboration with TK & The Holy Know-Nothings, which spent six weeks at #1 on the Americana Albums chart. Expansive yet intimate, the new record marks another chapter for Craigie while retaining the sincerity and conversational songwriting that have become central to his work.
 

Craigie returns to San Fran, Wellington on Thursday 15 April and The Tuning Fork, Auckland on Friday 16 April 2027, returning to the same venues that hosted his first New Zealand tour in 2025.
 

San Fran holds a Supervised License. Minors are welcome to attend events at San Fran so long as they are accompanied by a legal guardian at all times whilst at the venue.

events.name: The Curious Case of Benjamin Button The Musical
events.venue: St James Theatre, Wellington, New Zealand
events.long_description:
Every second counts. That’s the theme of The Curious Case of Benjamin Button. Having taken London and New York by storm, the hit musical is now making its way to Wellington, New Zealand. 

Described by WhatsOnStage as “The best British musical in decades” the show is an enchantingly beautiful and truly unordinary story. It follows Benjamin Button who is born old and bound to the fate of growing younger each day, Benjamin wants nothing more than to live a little life. But will he ever find a place to belong?   

The Olivier Award-winning musical is based on the 1922 short story by F Scott Fitzgerald. The story also inspired a 2008 movie. Now for the first time out of Broadway and the West End it travels to Australasia and Wellington has scored the premier. It brings a big heart, a foot-stomping score, and 15 remarkable actor-musicians who, among them, play 30 instruments. Get ready for a sweeping live score and a show epic in scale but intimate in feeling.

events.long_description:
Presented by: Destroy All Lines

St. Paul & The Broken Bones are a powerhouse soul ensemble from Alabama known for their electrifying live shows and impassioned vocals. Formed in Birmingham in 2011, the band features Paul Janeway (vocals), Jesse Phillips (bass), Browan Lollar (guitar), Kevin Leon (drums), Al Gamble (keyboards), Allen Branstetter (trumpet), Chad Fisher (trombone), and Amari Ansari (saxophone).

Their new self-titled sixth album marks a creative renewal—melding the band’s adventurous spirit with a return to soulful, song-focused roots. Recorded at the legendary FAME Studios and produced by Eg White (Adele, Celine Dion), the record blends psych-funk grooves, gospel-tinged ballads, and cinematic rock flourishes. Tracks like “Sushi and Coca-Cola” and “Going Back” reflect both personal introspection and the band’s deepened identity after a decade of evolution.

St. Paul & The Broken Bones have shared stages with The Rolling Stones, Lizzo, and Black Pumas, and performed at major festivals like Coachella, Glastonbury, Lollapalooza, and Bonnaroo. Even Sir Elton John took notice, inviting them to perform at his Oscar party. Blending rock & roll, soul, R&B, and more, the band continues to captivate audiences around the world.

events.id: Kia Mau--Wellington NZ
events.name: Kia Mau
events.long_description:
Kia Mau is an arts festival that showcases innovative Indigenous performances. Held every two years, the festival lights up Wellington's winter. See contemporary performances by leading Tāngata Whenua , Tāngata Moana, and global Indigenous artists. The two-week festival includes dance, theatre, music, and visual art. Audiences can expect to be challenged and thrilled by new work from Aotearoa and beyond.
Kia Mau was first held in 2015, founded by two leading Aotearoa creatives. Hone Kouka (Ngāti Porou, Ngāti Kahungunu, Ngāti Raukawa, Kai Tahu) is the Artistic Director and Chief Executive. Mīria George (Ngāti Kearoa, Ngāti Tuara, Ngāti Awa, Ngāti Kūki ‘Āirani) is the Executive Director.
Hone and Mīria describe themselves as innovators. They push boundaries, redefine forms, and forge new paths. They say the festival is not just a platform for presentations, it’s a hub for kōrero and whanaungatanga . The festival has a strong influence on many artists and plays an important role in shaping New Zealand’s contemporary arts scene. “Kia Mau has continued to thrive because of the imagination and commitment of our artists. And of us to them,” says Mīria.

Tribute band The Beatles Anthology is coming to The Opera House in June. For two hours, the show will take you down the long and winding road of The Beatles’ greatest hits. Expect the band to cover the era of matching suits and mop haircuts to the later experimental days. The four singers stand out for their authenticity and attention to detail, bringing the essence of The Beatles to life in every show. 

You might hear classics like Let It Be, Lucy in the Sky with Diamonds, and Yellow Submarine. Often regarded as the most influential band in popular music, The Beatles need little introduction. The Beatles Anthology brings a performance that captures the spirit of the Fab Four to Wellington audiences. This concert has the costumes, the hairstyles, the banter, and the gear. It’s not The Beatles, but it’ll feel like it.

events.name: NZSLTA Conference
events.venue: Wellington, New Zealand
events.long_description:
NZSLTA Conference
We are excited to announce that the NZSLTA conference will take place at Victoria University of Wellington.

2027 is a big anniversary year!

We invite you to join us to celebrate three milestones in NZSL teaching history:

👐35 years since the first formation of NZSLTA (1992)

📖 30 years since the launch of the Dictionary of NZSL (1997)

🎓30 years of the Certificate in Deaf Studies: Teaching NZSL at VUW (1997)

Over this time, the NZSL teaching profession has grown and had a huge impact on breaking down communication and attitude barriers for the Deaf community. Growth of this field has also supported many new professional opportunities and services.

This conference is an opportunity for NZSL teachers to celebrate our progress, reflect on current challenges and think together about future directions. The conference theme is:

“Energising NZSL Teachers”

We aim to make an exciting conference programme that will show the depth and diversity of knowledge, skills and creativity in our teaching community.

We look forward seeing you here in Wellington!

events.id: Bat Out of Hell — The Musical-Michael Fowler Centre, Wellington, New Zealand-Wellington NZ
events.name: Bat Out of Hell — The Musical
events.venue: Michael Fowler Centre, Wellington, New Zealand
events.long_description:
The explosive stage show, Bat Out of Hell — The Musical, swoops onto the stage of Wellington’s Michael Fowler Centre in August 2027. The musical is based around songs from Meat Loaf’s 1977 album ‘Bat Out of Hell’. It marks the 50th anniversary of its release.  Featuring an all-Kiwi cast and a live band, it covers a uniquely theatrical song list from the 50-year-old album. Expect a fun, chaotic musical that defies traditional theatre rules.   

A wild, post-apocalyptic world offers a backdrop for the show. The story follows Strat, an 18-year-old rebel leader of a gang called The Lost, who falls in love with Raven, the sheltered daughter of the city's tyrannical boss, Falco. Packed with massive tunes, you will hear hits like ‘I’d Do Anything for Love (But I Won’t Do That)’, ‘Paradise by the Dashboard Light’, ‘Two Out of Three Ain't Bad’, ‘Dead Ringer for Love’, ‘It’s All Coming Back to Me Now’, and the title track.   

The Bat Out of Hell album evolved from writer and composer Jim Steinman’s early university workshops. Despite initially being rejected by mainstream radio, it became one of the biggest-selling albums in history. It’s an album that takes up space: big, brash, and loud, like the musical itself.   

Ben McDonald, the producer of the musicals Chicago and Menopause the Musical, teams up with Stewart and Tricia Macpherson (The Best Exotic Marigold Hotel and Green Day’s American Idiot musical) to produce the New Zealand tour.

events.id: Black Ferns vs British and Irish Lions-Hnry Stadium, Wellington, New Zealand-Wellington NZ
events.name: Black Ferns vs British and Irish Lions
events.venue: Hnry Stadium, Wellington, New Zealand
events.long_description:
The first-ever Howden British and Irish Lions women‘s series is coming to Aotearoa in 2027. With five games across the country, Wellington is to play host to one of three Test games. The competition is sure to be fierce and the atmosphere electric. 
Sitting at the halfway point between Rugby World Cups, the tour will offer high-calibre clashes between two rugby powerhouses. Ben Calveley, CEO of The British & Irish Lions, said the tour marks “something truly special for the women’s game.” With the first-ever tour title on the table, you can expect both teams to leave it all on the field. Let‘s fill the cake tin with stomping feet and edge-of-your-seat screams. The Wellington game is Test number two of the series, so pull on your jersey, warm up your pipes and get ready for Black Ferns fever to sweep the city. 
Tickets go on sale late 2026.

events.venue: The Opera House, Wellington, New Zealand
events.long_description:
Celebrate the creative genius and musical talent of one of the greatest pop singers. The Michael Jackson HIStory Show promises to be a riveting live performance. The full-scale production at the Opera House pays tribute to one of the most significant cultural figures of the 20th century. Expect a stellar live band, choreographed dancers, and authentic costumes. 

Garth Field is at the centre of this performance. He’s often described as electrifying in his role as Michael. Garth is a triple-threat performer with impeccable vocals, dancing, and acting. 

The show tracks Michael’s journey from his early days as a member of the Jackson 5 to his groundbreaking theatrics in the 80s. It goes on to acknowledge his continued domination of pop culture into the 21st century. Hear all the hits like Thriller, Billie Jean, Bad, Beat It, Don’t Stop Til You Get Enough, They Don’t Really Care About Us, and many more.
